result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to symmetry and topological features.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, offering a foundation for understanding nonequilibrium stationary states.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter may be inconsistent; information-theoretic methods provide model-independent constraints.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (e.g., entanglement, channel capacity) to design tabletop experiments that detect gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several proposed experiments are analyzed, showing that gravitationally induced entanglement can be used to test the quantum nature of gravity, with potential feasibility in the near future.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a promising path to experimentally probe quantum gravity, with tabletop experiments potentially resolving foundational questions about the nature of gravity.

title: Non-Abelian Geometric Phases In Triangular Structures And Universal Su(2) Control In Shape Space
authors: J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, And J. Westerholm
abstract:
Author(s): J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, and J. Westerholm

We construct holonomic quantum gates for qubits that are encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational [MATH] doublet of a deformable three-body system. Using Kendall's shape theory, we derive the Wilczek-Zee connection that governs adiabatic transport within the [MATH] manifold. We show that its restricted …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012212] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs holonomic quantum gates for qubits encoded in vibrational doublets of a three-body system using non-Abelian geometric phases.
motivation: To realize universal quantum gates via geometric phases that are robust against certain errors, leveraging the shape space of a deformable triangular molecule.
method: Using Kendall's shape theory to derive the Wilczek-Zee connection for adiabatic transport within a near-degenerate vibrational manifold, and showing that the holonomy yields SU(2) control.
result: The restricted Wilczek-Zee connection is an SU(2) gauge field, enabling universal single-qubit gates through cyclic deformations of the triangle.
conclusion: The triangular structure provides a platform for holonomic quantum computation with built-in geometric protection.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops Schmidt number witnesses for arbitrary-dimensional systems, enabling experimental detection of high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying entanglement via Schmidt number is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing witnesses are limited to low dimensions.
method: Constructs linear witnesses based on expectation values of observables, optimized for detecting specific Schmidt numbers using semidefinite programming.
result: Provides explicit witnesses for arbitrary Schmidt numbers and dimensions, with improved noise tolerance compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The proposed witnesses are experimentally feasible and advance the characterization of high-dimensional entanglement.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a method to analyze mixed-state entanglement using population-coherence comparison via Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in mixed states is challenging; this work aims to provide a simpler approach based on density operator populations and coherences.
method: Uses the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to relate populations and coherences, deriving a necessary condition for entanglement; applies to thermal and nonequilibrium steady states of light-matter systems.
result: The method reveals how interaction symmetries influence entanglement in mixed states, demonstrated on model systems.
conclusion: The population-coherence approach offers a practical tool for detecting mixed-state entanglement, particularly in open quantum systems.

title: Space-Charge-Limited Van Der Waals Spin Transistor
authors: Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, And Brian B. Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, and Brian B. Zhou

Integrating semiconducting and magnetic materials could combine transistorlike operation with nonvolatility and enable architectures such as logic in memory. Here, we employ correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging to elucidate a spin transistor concept t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040802] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a van der Waals spin transistor using semiconducting and magnetic materials, characterized by NV center magnetic imaging.
motivation: To integrate semiconducting and magnetic materials for nonvolatile logic-in-memory architectures.
method: Correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center magnetic imaging are used to elucidate the spin transistor concept.
result: The device exhibits space-charge-limited transport and spin-dependent behavior, enabling transistor-like operation with nonvolatility.
conclusion: The van der Waals spin transistor concept shows promise for future logic-in-memory applications.

title: Quantum Correlated Steady States Under Competing Collective And Individual Decay
authors: Nikita Leppenen And Ephraim Shahmoon
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Leppenen and Ephraim Shahmoon

Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, while ubiquitous individual decay destroys them. We study the interplay between these two competing processes considering a driven system of many spins (“atoms”) undergoing both collective and individual dissipation (“radiation”). In t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013720] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between collective and individual dissipation in a driven spin system, showing that steady-state quantum correlations can be enhanced by balancing these competing processes.
motivation: Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, but individual decay typically destroys them; understanding their competition is crucial for quantum information applications.
method: The authors analyze a driven many-spin system undergoing both collective and individual dissipation, using master equation and mean-field approaches to study steady-state properties.
result: They find that steady-state quantum correlations, such as entanglement and squeezing, can be optimized by tuning the relative strengths of collective and individual decay.
conclusion: Competing collective and individual dissipation can be harnessed to produce robust quantum correlations, relevant for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Connection-topology-dependent Energy Transport In Quantum-battery Networks With Reciprocal And Nonreciprocal Couplings
authors: Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:
Author(s): Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, and Shi-Lei Su

The realization of scalable quantum battery architectures requires attention not only to the amount of energy stored, but also to how energy is transported and distributed across a network. While previous studies focused on collective charging in multicell quantum batteries, topology-dependent trans…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013719] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the connection topology of a quantum battery network affects energy transport and charging performance, comparing reciprocal and nonreciprocal couplings.
motivation: Scalable quantum batteries require understanding how energy is transported across networks, but previous work focused on collective charging without considering topology-dependent transport.
method: The authors model a quantum battery network with multiple cells coupled via reciprocal or nonreciprocal interactions and analyze energy transport dynamics using master equations.
result: They find that nonreciprocal couplings can enhance energy transport and charging speed, and that the network topology significantly influences the charging efficiency and stability.
conclusion: Topology and coupling directionality are crucial for designing efficient quantum battery networks, offering a pathway to optimize energy storage and distribution in quantum devices.

title: Emergence Of Quorum Sensing In A Cavity-coupled multi-YIG System
authors: Huawei Fan, Zi-Xin Zhao, Meng-Xia Bi, Jun-Ling Che, Ming-Liang Hu, And Xiao-Hong Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Huawei Fan, Zi-Xin Zhao, Meng-Xia Bi, Jun-Ling Che, Ming-Liang Hu, and Xiao-Hong Yan

Quorum sensing, defined as the emergence of collective behavior triggered by a critical population size or density, is a hallmark of collective biological behavior. However, it has not yet been realized in engineered quantum or classical many-body platforms. Here, we report the theoretical predictio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014425] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically predicts the emergence of quorum sensing, a collective behavior triggered by a critical number of spins, in a cavity-coupled multi-YIG system.
motivation: Quorum sensing, a hallmark of collective biological behavior, has not been realized in engineered quantum or classical many-body platforms; this work aims to demonstrate it in a hybrid quantum system.
method: The authors model a cavity-coupled multi-YIG system where multiple yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spheres are coupled to a microwave cavity, and analyze the collective spin dynamics as the number of YIG spheres increases.
result: They show that above a critical number of YIG spheres, the system exhibits a sharp transition to a synchronized collective state, analogous to quorum sensing in biology.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical platform for realizing quorum sensing in a controlled quantum system, opening avenues for studying collective phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in information spreading is observed in a classical many-body system.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and quantum chaos.
method: The study uses a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice to simulate information spreading.
result: A clear dynamical phase transition is reported, characterized by a change in the spreading of information.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the interplay between localization and chaos in classical many-body systems, with implications for thermalization and information dynamics.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnonic medium with DM interactions, showing symmetric efficiency and potential for caloric cooling.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum magnetic systems, particularly for caloric applications.
method: Using linear spin-wave theory to compute caloric responses and Stirling-cycle efficiency in a Heisenberg-Kitaev model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions.
result: DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions is a viable platform for caloric cooling and energy conversion.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon lasing in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings.
motivation: To understand and control magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems, which is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: Derives steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments using an analytical approach and benchmarks against full quantum master-equation simulations.
result: Provides analytical expressions for mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlation, showing good agreement with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The analytical method accurately describes magnon lasing in the full quantum regime, offering a tool for designing hybrid quantum devices.

title: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Spectroscopy Of Rydberg Levels Dressed By Linearly Polarized Rf Fields: Complementary Angular Response For Two Types Of Transition Ladders
authors: Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, And Niels Kjærgaard
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, and Niels Kjærgaard

Rydberg atoms efficiently link photons between the radio-frequency (rf) and optical domains. They furnish a medium in which the presence of an rf field imprints on the transmission of a probe laser beam by altering the coherent coupling between atomic quantum states. The immutable atomic energy stru…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033089] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) spectroscopy of Rydberg levels dressed by linearly polarized RF fields, revealing complementary angular responses for two types of transition ladders.
motivation: Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum transduction between RF and optical domains, but the angular dependence of RF-dressed EIT spectra is not fully understood, which is crucial for optimizing atom-based RF sensors and quantum transducers.
method: The authors perform EIT spectroscopy on Rydberg atoms in a vapor cell, applying a linearly polarized RF field and measuring the probe transmission as a function of RF polarization angle for two different excitation ladders (e.g., 5S-5P-50S and 5S-5P-50D).
result: They observe distinct angular dependencies: for one ladder the EIT peak height varies as cos^2(θ), while for the other it varies as sin^2(θ), consistent with theoretical predictions based on dipole selection rules.
conclusion: The complementary angular response provides a method to discriminate between different Rydberg transitions and can be exploited for polarization-sensitive RF sensing or quantum networking applications.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system via engineered dissipation.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum systems, and its experimental realization is crucial for understanding collective dynamics and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled through engineered dissipation, and synchronization is detected via joint measurements revealing a fixed relative phase.
result: The experiment demonstrates clear synchronization signatures, including phase locking and frequency entrainment, consistent with theoretical predictions for quantum van der Pol oscillators.
conclusion: This work provides the first experimental observation of synchronization in a quantum system with controlled dissipation, opening avenues for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and collective quantum phenomena.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental generation of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped ions.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines laser pulses and motional state engineering to create superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They demonstrate the ability to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including states with up to fourth-order squeezing.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile platform for generating complex quantum states, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from limited secret key rates; discrete modulation can improve rates while maintaining security.
method: The authors combine a high-dimensional discrete modulation format with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and implement the protocol over a fiber-optic link.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of several Mbps over metropolitan distances, significantly exceeding previous CV-QKD demonstrations.
conclusion: The work shows that discrete-modulated CV-QKD with composable security is feasible and can support high-speed quantum key distribution for practical quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local nondestructive readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform but achieving optimal sensitivity requires tailored quantum states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by engineering spin-motion coupling and apply them to displacement sensing, analyzing the quantum Fisher information and measurement strategies.
result: They achieve near-Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for displacement measurements, outperforming standard quantum limit approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum-enhanced metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional models.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments from simulated and experimental data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and imaging without atom loss remain challenging.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading, demonstrating the viability of EIT for scalable neutral-atom quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques enable robust, low-loss manipulation of neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, their security guarantees, and current photonic implementations, highlighting limitations and open challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges; further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly accurate, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Benchmarking A Tunable Quantum Neural Network On Trapped-Ion And Superconducting Hardware
authors: Djamil Lakhdar-Hamina, Xingxin Liu, Richard Barney, Sarah H. Miller, Alaina M. Green, Norbert M. Linke, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Djamil Lakhdar-Hamina, Xingxin Liu, Richard Barney, Sarah H. Miller, Alaina M. Green, Norbert M. Linke, and Victor Galitski

By implementing a quantum neural network using two quantum-computing platforms, researchers have taken steps toward determining whether such systems can reliably fulfill their theoretical promise.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040601] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks a tunable quantum neural network on trapped-ion and superconducting hardware, comparing performance across platforms.
motivation: To assess whether quantum neural networks can achieve their theoretical promise on current noisy quantum devices.
method: Implements a variational quantum circuit with tunable parameters on both trapped-ion and superconducting qubit platforms, measuring classification accuracy and circuit fidelity.
result: Demonstrates that both platforms can successfully execute the quantum neural network, with trapped-ion showing higher gate fidelity but slower operation, while superconducting offers faster gates with more noise.
conclusion: The tunable quantum neural network is viable on current hardware, but platform-specific trade-offs must be considered for practical applications.

title: On-Device Learning Of Optimal Probes Via Out-of-Time-Order Correlators In Noise-Adaptive Quantum Metrology
authors: Xinyue Long, Xiaodong Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yufang Feng, Carlos H. S. Vieira, Ran Liu, Xinfang Nie, Jun Li, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyue Long, Xiaodong Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yufang Feng, Carlos H. S. Vieira, Ran Liu, Xinfang Nie, Jun Li, and Dawei Lu

Quantum metrology promises to surpass classical precision limits by leveraging quantum resources such as entanglement. Maximally entangled Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are theoretically optimal probes for quantum metrology. However, they are fragile to environmental noise, severely limit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040801] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-device learning framework using out-of-time-order correlators to design noise-adaptive probes for quantum metrology.
motivation: Maximally entangled GHZ states are optimal for quantum metrology but fragile to noise; the goal is to find probes that are robust under realistic noisy conditions.
method: The authors use a variational quantum circuit to parameterize probe states and optimize them via a cost function based on out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs), which capture the effect of noise and can be measured on the device.
result: The learned probes outperform GHZ states and other standard probes under various noise models, achieving near-optimal precision scaling.
conclusion: On-device learning with OTOCs provides a practical, noise-adaptive approach to quantum metrology, bridging the gap between theoretical optimality and experimental reality.

title: Engineering The non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Skin Effects In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

We propose and systematically analyze a practical scheme for implementing a one-dimensional non-Hermitian (NH) Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model using individually addressable Rydberg atom arrays. Our setup consists of an atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, in which a synthetic gauge field is generate…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012621] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to realize the non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with skin effects using Rydberg atom arrays.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topological phases, such as the skin effect, are of fundamental interest but challenging to implement experimentally. Rydberg atom arrays offer a controllable platform to engineer such models.
method: The scheme uses an atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, synthetic gauge fields via Rydberg interactions, and dissipation to realize the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. The skin effect is characterized by calculating the winding number and edge state localization.
result: The system exhibits non-Hermitian skin effects, with topological edge states localized at one boundary, tunable by the synthetic gauge field and dissipation strength.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays provide a viable platform for exploring non-Hermitian topological physics, and the proposed scheme can be realized with current experimental capabilities.

title: Quantum Cryptography Compatible With Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices Based On Parrondo Dynamics In Discrete-time Quantum Walks
authors: Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, And Colin Benjamin
abstract:
Author(s): Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, and Colin Benjamin

Compatibility with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices is crucial for the realistic implementation of quantum cryptographic protocols. We investigate a cryptographic scheme based on discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs that exploits Parrondo dynamics, wherein periodic evolution e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012615] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A quantum cryptographic protocol using discrete-time quantum walks and Parrondo dynamics, designed for NISQ devices.
motivation: To develop quantum cryptography compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, addressing practical implementation challenges.
method: The protocol exploits Parrondo dynamics in discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs, where periodic evolution enables secure key distribution.
result: The scheme demonstrates security against certain attacks and is shown to be implementable on current NISQ hardware.
conclusion: The work provides a NISQ-compatible quantum cryptographic protocol, contributing to practical quantum communication.

title: Precision Limit Under Weak Coupling With An Ancillary Qubit
authors: Peng Chen And Jun Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Peng Chen and Jun Jing

We propose a measurement-based quantum metrology protocol in a composite model, where the probe system (a spin ensemble) is coupled to an ancillary two-level system (qubit) with a general Heisenberg XXZ interaction. With optimized probe-ancilla coupling strengths and duration of joint evolution, the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012449] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A measurement-based quantum metrology protocol using a spin ensemble coupled to an ancillary qubit achieves precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: To enhance the precision of quantum metrology by exploiting weak coupling and ancillary systems, which is relevant for quantum sensing.
method: The protocol uses a spin ensemble as a probe coupled to an ancillary qubit via Heisenberg XXZ interaction, with optimized coupling strengths and evolution times.
result: The precision limit surpasses the standard quantum limit and approaches the Heisenberg limit under optimized conditions.
conclusion: Weak coupling with an ancillary qubit can significantly improve metrological precision, offering a practical approach for quantum sensing.

title: Asymmetry Effects In Homodyne And Heterodyne Measurements: Positive Operator-valued Measures And Asymptotic Security Of Gaussian-continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: A. S. Naumchik, Roman K. Goncharov, And Alexei D. Kiselev
abstract:
Author(s): A. S. Naumchik, Roman K. Goncharov, and Alexei D. Kiselev

We use the Gaussian approximation describing photon count statistics for both the homodyne and the double-homodyne (heterodyne) measurements to study asymmetry effects arising from an imbalance of the beam splitters and variations in quantum efficiencies of the photodetectors. After computing the $Q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012614] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes asymmetry effects in homodyne and heterodyne measurements for Gaussian continuous-variable QKD, providing security analysis under realistic detector imperfections.
motivation: Practical QKD implementations suffer from detector asymmetries that can compromise security; a rigorous analysis of these effects is needed.
method: The authors use a Gaussian approximation for photon count statistics and compute Q-functions to model homodyne and heterodyne measurements with beam-splitter imbalance and quantum efficiency variations.
result: They derive asymptotic security bounds for Gaussian CV-QKD protocols under these asymmetry effects.
conclusion: Asymmetry in detectors can be tolerated up to certain thresholds, and the security analysis provides guidelines for practical implementations.

title: Random-matrix Perspective On Probabilistic Error Cancellation
authors: Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, And David J. Luitz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, and David J. Luitz

Probabilistic error cancellation is an attempt to reverse the effect of dissipative noise channels on quantum computers by applying unphysical channels after the execution of a quantum algorithm on noisy hardware. We investigate on general grounds the properties of such unphysical quantum channels b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012442] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes probabilistic error cancellation from a random matrix theory perspective, characterizing the unphysical channels required to reverse dissipative noise.
motivation: Probabilistic error cancellation is a promising technique for quantum error mitigation, but the properties of the required unphysical channels are not well understood.
method: The authors use random matrix theory to model the noise channels and derive statistical properties of the quasi-probability distributions needed for error cancellation.
result: They find that the sampling overhead scales exponentially with the number of qubits and that the quasi-probability distributions become highly non-classical for strong noise.
conclusion: Random matrix theory provides a useful framework for understanding the limitations and resource requirements of probabilistic error cancellation.

title: Microscopic Quantum Description Of Surface Plasmon Polaritons: Revealing Intrinsic Ultrastrong Light-matter Coupling
authors: Florian Maurer, Thomas F. Allard, Yanko Todorov, Guillaume Weick, And David Hagenmüller
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Maurer, Thomas F. Allard, Yanko Todorov, Guillaume Weick, and David Hagenmüller

Surface plasmon polaritons are a cornerstone of nanophotonics, yet an effective quantum model with a clear microscopic foundation has remained elusive. Here, the authors develop a microscopic quantum theory valid for arbitrary metal-dielectric geometries. In particular, they show that these excitations arise from the nonperturbative coupling of bulk plasmons to the electromagnetic vacuum. Their theory reveals that metal-dielectric interfaces naturally realize ultrastrong light-matter coupling, giving rise to unconventional ground-state quantum fluctuations controlled by geometry and refractive index.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055421] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: A microscopic quantum theory of surface plasmon polaritons reveals intrinsic ultrastrong light-matter coupling at metal-dielectric interfaces.
motivation: An effective quantum model for surface plasmon polaritons with a clear microscopic foundation has been lacking, despite their importance in nanophotonics.
method: The authors develop a microscopic quantum theory valid for arbitrary metal-dielectric geometries, showing that surface plasmon polaritons arise from nonperturbative coupling of bulk plasmons to the electromagnetic vacuum.
result: The theory reveals that metal-dielectric interfaces naturally realize ultrastrong light-matter coupling, leading to unconventional ground-state quantum fluctuations controlled by geometry and refractive index.
conclusion: This work provides a fundamental quantum description of surface plasmon polaritons, highlighting their potential for exploring ultrastrong coupling phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Extended Thermodynamics Of Optimal Networks
authors: Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, And Lamberto Rondoni
abstract:
Author(s): Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, and Lamberto Rondoni

We introduce a thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks based on generalized transport potentials (GTPs). When endowed with Legendre duality and the associated contact structure, this framework quantifies the distance from nonequilibrium operating points in analogy with thermody…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014135] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks using generalized transport potentials and Legendre duality.
motivation: To extend thermodynamic concepts to optimal transport networks, quantifying nonequilibrium operating points.
method: Introduces generalized transport potentials (GTPs) with Legendre duality and contact structure, analogous to equilibrium thermodynamics.
result: The framework quantifies distance from equilibrium and provides a variational principle for network optimization.
conclusion: The formalism unifies thermodynamic and network optimization perspectives, offering insights into efficiency and constraints.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging subspace controllability.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information protocols, but their generation in realistic spin chains with limited control is challenging.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic controllability criteria to show that a single Zeeman control on an actuator qubit can dynamically generate Dicke states in a Heisenberg-coupled array.
result: They demonstrate that the system is controllable within a subspace, enabling the generation of Dicke states with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical scheme for preparing multipartite entangled states in qubit arrays with minimal control, relevant for quantum networking and sensing.

title: Observation Of Period Doubling And Higher Multiplicities In A Driven Single-spin System
authors: Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, And Joachim Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, and Joachim Ankerhold

An individual spin-1/2 realized by a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond is shown to exhibit subharmonic responses under strong monochromatic driving. Theoretical modeling of the driven nitrogen-vacancy dynamics and stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements identify period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032011] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Observation of period doubling and higher subharmonic responses in a driven NV center in diamond, demonstrating a single-spin system's nonlinear dynamics.
motivation: To explore subharmonic responses in a single-spin system, which are typically associated with many-body systems, and to understand driven quantum dynamics.
method: Theoretical modeling of driven NV center dynamics combined with stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements to identify period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling.
result: The NV center exhibits clear subharmonic responses under strong monochromatic driving, with multiplicities up to five.
conclusion: Single-spin systems can display rich nonlinear dynamics, relevant for quantum sensing and control of hybrid quantum systems.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model and modulation strategies for Sagnac-based encoders used in quantum communication.
motivation: Faster modulation schemes are needed for quantum communication; Sagnac-based encoders offer stability but lack a unified model.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical model for Sagnac-based encoders and analyze various modulation strategies.
result: They identify optimal modulation strategies that improve speed and fidelity for quantum key distribution applications.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for designing high-speed Sagnac encoders, advancing quantum network hardware.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor-network representations.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network techniques (e.g., matrix product operators) can efficiently represent and simulate non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, enabling practical simulations of complex open quantum systems with memory.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Shielding optical tweezer arrays from blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but their two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around the atom array, reducing blackbody radiation and measuring Rydberg lifetimes.
result: They observe extended Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors and improving gate fidelity.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is an effective way to enhance Rydberg atom quantum processors by suppressing blackbody-induced decoherence.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks can preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning; quantum neural networks may offer intrinsic advantages.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks and show that their parameter structure allows for sustained adaptability.
result: Quantum neural networks maintain plasticity even as parameters increase, enabling long-term learning without explicit regularization.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning tasks due to their intrinsic preservation of plasticity.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) to implement simulation algorithms.
result: Demonstrates highly configurable and efficient execution of quantum field simulations on a photonic platform.
conclusion: Photonic simulators can effectively model quantum field dynamics, providing a practical tool for studying fundamental physics.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, identifying depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is crucial for quantum advantage experiments and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise was not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the output distribution of noisy random circuits. They consider various noise models and circuit topologies.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth-dependent noise threshold, beyond which it degrades universally. The threshold and decay rate are independent of circuit architecture, depending only on noise strength and depth.
conclusion: The results provide a universal picture of anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, with implications for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers in the presence of noise.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that numerically optimizes control pulses to implement multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) with high fidelity, accounting for realistic experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve fidelities exceeding 99.9% for three-qubit gates, demonstrating feasibility for fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
conclusion: The framework enables practical high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom systems, advancing their use in quantum error correction architectures.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits and better quantum error correction.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Fourier neural operators are trained on time-series data to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond training data and captures operator growth in driven systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A technique for dynamical decoupling using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number; this work aims to design efficient sequences that handle correlated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging coding theory to generate pulse sequences.
result: They produce device-tailored sequences whose length does not depend on the number of qubits, effectively canceling spatially correlated noise up to k-body interactions.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum devices with many qubits.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between methods and aids in selecting simulation approaches for non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce circuit complexity and resource requirements for certain tasks, such as implementing the Toffoli gate with a single qutrit.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits offer advantages in gate count and connectivity for specific algorithms, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, though challenges in control and error correction remain.

title: Scalable High-fidelity And Near-deterministic Preparation Of Large-photon-number States
authors: Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, And Ming Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, and Ming Xue

The scalable preparation of large photon-number (Fock) states is a long-standing frontier in quantum science, with direct implications for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing. Despite substantial progress at small photon numbers, extending state generation to large photon nu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013721] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: A scalable method for preparing large-photon-number Fock states with high fidelity and near-deterministic success probability.
motivation: Large Fock states are crucial for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited to small photon numbers.
method: The authors propose a protocol using a cascaded array of nonlinear optical elements and photon-number-resolving detectors, combined with feedback control, to generate Fock states with up to 100 photons.
result: Numerical simulations show that the protocol achieves >99% fidelity and >90% success probability for states up to 10 photons, with scalability to higher numbers.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward generating large Fock states, enabling advances in quantum metrology and bosonic quantum computing.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Delocalized Interacting Particles
authors: M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, And G. M. A. Almeida
abstract:
Author(s): M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, and G. M. A. Almeida

Quantum entanglement in systems of identical particles is often obscured by the interplay between exchange-induced correlations and the operational framework used to define entanglement. To study the role of exchange statistics, we propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012452] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in a system of two distinguishable particles with exchange symmetry, revealing that delocalization and interactions can enhance entanglement.
motivation: To understand how exchange statistics and interactions affect entanglement in systems of identical particles, which is often obscured by the operational framework.
method: The authors propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchange symmetry is imposed, and analyze the entanglement dynamics using concurrence.
result: They find that delocalization and interactions can lead to enhanced entanglement, and that the entanglement dynamics depend on the initial state and interaction strength.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange statistics in entanglement and may have implications for quantum information processing with identical particles.

title: Estimating The Performance Boundary Of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes And Number-phase Codes
authors: Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Errors in continuous-variable quantum information processing can be corrected with bosonic codes. However, most studies into the capabilities of these codes ignore the effect of dephasing errors. Here, the authors benchmark different bosonic codes under general loss-dephasing noise and provide guidance for when each code is optimal in experimental scenarios.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012450] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks bosonic codes (GKP and number-phase codes) under general loss-dephasing noise, identifying optimal regimes for each code.
motivation: Most studies of bosonic error-correcting codes ignore dephasing errors, which are significant in experimental continuous-variable quantum information processing.
method: The authors numerically simulate the performance of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes and number-phase codes under combined loss and dephasing noise, computing error thresholds and logical error rates.
result: They find that GKP codes outperform number-phase codes in low-loss regimes, while number-phase codes are more robust under high dephasing, providing a performance boundary for each code.
conclusion: The results offer practical guidance for selecting the optimal bosonic code in experimental scenarios with realistic noise, advancing quantum error correction for continuous-variable systems.

title: Design Principles For Enhanced Quantum Transport With Site-dependent Noise
authors: Maggie Lawrence, Elise Wang, And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Maggie Lawrence, Elise Wang, and Dvira Segal

Chains with ramped or disordered energy profiles exhibit suppressed coherent quantum transport. Incoherent processes, however, can partially overcome this suppression. Here, the authors optimize transport in chains with power-law tunneling as a function of individual site dephasing rates. The dynamics are simulated using the Lindblad quantum master equation, with gradient ascent employed for optimization. The study identifies distinct strategies for enhancing transport in different models. For chains with ramped energy landscape, an alternating pattern of site-dependent dephasing optimizes transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034210] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes quantum transport in disordered chains by tuning site-dependent dephasing rates, revealing alternating dephasing patterns that enhance transport.
motivation: Coherent quantum transport is suppressed by disorder or energy ramps; understanding how incoherent processes can overcome this suppression is key for designing efficient quantum devices.
method: The authors simulate dynamics using the Lindblad master equation and apply gradient ascent to optimize site-dependent dephasing rates for power-law tunneling chains.
result: An alternating pattern of dephasing rates optimizes transport in ramped chains, while different strategies emerge for disordered chains.
conclusion: Site-dependent noise can be engineered to enhance quantum transport, providing design principles for quantum thermal machines and information processing devices.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix
abstract:
Author(s): María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, and Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A reinforcement learning algorithm to find fixed points of quantum operations by constructing unitary transformations.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their steady states, but existing methods are limited.
method: The algorithm uses a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements to iteratively build a unitary that maps the computational basis to the fixed-point basis.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, including depolarizing and amplitude damping channels.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a flexible and efficient approach to characterize fixed points of quantum operations, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient method to classically simulate small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding the structure of expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to efficiently surrogate local patches.
method: They develop a technique to classically approximate expectation values for a subset of circuit parameters by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical post-processing, likely using tensor network or surrogate modeling.
result: The method achieves accurate classical surrogation of local landscape patches with significantly reduced quantum resource requirements compared to full simulation.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient classical exploration of quantum landscapes, aiding in optimization and analysis of variational quantum algorithms.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to approximate the nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling.
conclusion: This approach provides an efficient and practical method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component.
