By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillations in a minimal negative feedback loop with phase separation, using a combined mean-field and particle-based model.
motivation: Oscillations are a hallmark of nonequilibrium biological processes, and understanding how phase separation influences them is important for cellular regulation.
method: The authors couple ordinary differential equations with a particle-based model to analyze a degradation-mediated negative feedback loop where the final species degrades the first, incorporating phase separation effects.
result: Phase separation can induce oscillations in the feedback loop, altering the dynamics compared to the well-mixed case.
conclusion: Phase separation is a key mechanism for generating oscillatory behavior in biochemical networks, with implications for cellular function.

title: Zero-noise Extrapolation Via Cyclic Permutations Of Quantum Circuit Layouts
authors: Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, And Kirill Lakhmanskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, and Kirill Lakhmanskiy

Increasing the utility of currently available noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires developing efficient methods to mitigate hardware errors. In this work we propose a novel cyclic layout permutations based zero noise extrapolation (CLP-ZNE) protocol for such a task. The method le…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012620] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a zero-noise extrapolation error mitigation method using cyclic permutations of quantum circuit layouts.
motivation: NISQ devices require efficient error mitigation to improve utility; existing ZNE methods have limitations.
method: Cyclically permutes the layout of quantum circuits to vary noise levels and extrapolate to zero noise.
result: The CLP-ZNE protocol demonstrates improved error mitigation compared to standard ZNE on test circuits.
conclusion: Cyclic layout permutations offer a practical and effective approach for zero-noise extrapolation on NISQ devices.

title: Identifying Local Unitary Equivalence Based On Reduction Of Quantum States
authors: Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, and Shao-Ming Fei

Local unitary equivalence is central to entanglement quantification and classification. Identifying the local unitary equivalence remains a formidable challenge. We address this problem for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate simple eigenvalues …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012451] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to determine local unitary equivalence for quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue using reduction of quantum states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is important for entanglement classification but remains challenging; the authors aim to simplify the problem for a specific class of states.
method: They reduce the problem to checking local unitary equivalence of the reduced density matrices of the nondegenerate eigenstates, using invariants derived from the reduced states.
result: They provide necessary and sufficient conditions for local unitary equivalence of the considered class of states, and illustrate with examples.
conclusion: The method simplifies the identification of local unitary equivalence for states with high degeneracy, contributing to entanglement theory.

title: Biased-noise Thresholds Of Zero-rate Holographic Codes With Tensor-network Decoding
authors: J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, And S. Feld
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, and S. Feld

A crucial insight for practical quantum error correction is that different types of errors, such as single-qubit Pauli operators, typically occur with different probabilities. Finding an optimal quantum code under such biased noise is a challenging problem, related to the (generally unknown) maximum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012447] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased-noise thresholds of zero-rate holographic codes using tensor-network decoding.
motivation: Practical quantum error correction requires codes optimized for biased noise, but finding optimal codes is challenging.
method: The authors analyze holographic quantum codes under biased noise models and employ tensor-network decoding algorithms.
result: They compute threshold error rates for various bias scenarios and identify code families with improved performance.
conclusion: Holographic codes can achieve high thresholds under biased noise, but the zero-rate nature limits practical applicability.

title: Variational Preparation Of Quantum Many-body Scars With Shallow Circuits
authors: Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, And Giuliano Benenti
abstract:
Author(s): Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, and Giuliano Benenti

We present and benchmark a type of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) which we denote [MATH]-VQE. It is designed to target midspectrum eigenstates and prepare quantum many-body scar states. The approach leverages the fact that noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices are limited in their ability to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012613] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) variant is introduced to prepare quantum many-body scar states using shallow circuits.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are non-thermal eigenstates that evade thermalization, but preparing them on near-term quantum devices is challenging due to circuit depth constraints.
method: The authors propose a modified VQE (M-VQE) that targets mid-spectrum eigenstates by optimizing a cost function that penalizes states far from the target energy window, using shallow variational circuits.
result: Numerical simulations demonstrate successful preparation of scar states in the PXP model and other systems, with high fidelity using circuits of modest depth.
conclusion: The method provides a practical approach to study quantum many-body scars on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices, though the contribution is incremental relative to existing VQE techniques.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation
authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, and Xiaoguang Wang

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals beyond mean-field theory using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation, revealing finite-size effects and decaying oscillations.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior is not well understood beyond mean-field approximations.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to analyze the open quantum system dynamics of boundary time crystals, going beyond mean-field theory.
result: They find that finite-size systems exhibit decaying oscillations that cannot be captured by mean-field theory, and characterize the crossover from persistent to decaying oscillations.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate description of boundary time crystals in finite systems, highlighting the importance of beyond-mean-field effects in dissipative quantum phases.

title: Two-parameter Family-Vicsek Scaling In A Dissipative Xxz Spin Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, Tamás Vicsek, And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, Tamás Vicsek, and Balázs Dóra

Family-Vicsek (FV) scaling provides an understanding for the growth and finite-size saturation of fluctuations in classical systems. Here, we extend the FV roughness to transferred segment magnetization after quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain with homogeneous gain and loss, starting f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055129] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends Family-Vicsek scaling to quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain, revealing two-parameter scaling of magnetization fluctuations.
motivation: To understand how classical surface growth scaling laws apply to quantum systems with dissipation, particularly the growth and saturation of fluctuations after a quench.
method: Studies the transferred segment magnetization after quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain with homogeneous gain and loss, using analytical and numerical methods to extract scaling exponents.
result: Identifies a two-parameter Family-Vicsek scaling regime with distinct dynamic and roughness exponents, showing that dissipation modifies the scaling behavior compared to closed systems.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that classical scaling concepts can be generalized to open quantum systems, providing a framework for characterizing non-equilibrium quantum dynamics with dissipation.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, and Stephen Hughes

We present a matrix product state (MPS) method for including decoherence processes in calculations involving waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices. The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state method for modeling decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: Accurate modeling of decoherence in waveguide QED is important for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive.
method: The authors use a collision quantum optics approach combined with matrix product states to efficiently simulate the many-body state of the waveguide including decoherence.
result: The MPS method accurately captures decoherence effects and scales favorably with system size compared to exact diagonalization.
conclusion: The proposed MPS method provides a practical tool for simulating decoherence in waveguide QED systems, enabling studies of larger and more realistic setups.

title: Molecular Quantum Control Algorithm Design By Reinforcement Learning
authors: Anastasia Pipi, Xuecheng Tao, Arianna Wu, Prineha Narang, And David R. Leibrandt
abstract:
Author(s): Anastasia Pipi, Xuecheng Tao, Arianna Wu, Prineha Narang, and David R. Leibrandt

Precision measurements of molecules offer an unparalleled paradigm to probe physics beyond the standard model. The rich internal structure within these molecules makes them exquisite sensors for detecting fundamental symmetry violations, local position invariance, and dark matter. While trapping and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033103] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design quantum control algorithms for molecular precision measurements.
motivation: Molecules are sensitive probes for fundamental physics, but controlling their quantum states is challenging.
method: Reinforcement learning is applied to optimize control pulses for molecular quantum systems.
result: The RL-based approach achieves high-fidelity control for molecular qubits.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning is a promising tool for designing quantum control in molecular systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator
authors: Xue Gao, Jun Xu, And Xiangming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xue Gao, Jun Xu, and Xiangming Hu

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a spinning resonator system to generate nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission via a two-mode cavity coupled to a two-level atom.
motivation: To realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission, which is important for quantum information processing and chiral quantum optics.
method: Uses a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, exploiting the Sagnac effect to break reciprocity and achieve directional emission of photon bundles.
result: Demonstrates efficient excitation of multiphoton bundle states with nonreciprocal behavior, where the emission direction depends on the rotation direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal multiphoton sources, with potential applications in quantum networks and on-chip photonic circuits.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to embed fault-tolerant quantum circuits on connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, optimizing for circuit depth and gate count.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring SWAP gates to implement long-distance interactions. Existing approaches often ignore fault tolerance constraints, leading to inefficient circuits.
method: The authors develop a compiler that maps logical circuits to physical hardware with limited connectivity, inserting SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity requirements while preserving fault tolerance. They use graph-based optimization to minimize overhead.
result: The method reduces the number of SWAP gates and circuit depth compared to naive approaches, enabling fault-tolerant circuits on realistic hardware topologies.
conclusion: Efficient SWAP insertion is crucial for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing on near-term devices, and the proposed compiler achieves significant improvements.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system and quantifies the advantage via cross-entropy benchmarking.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is verifiable and utilizable, with performance exceeding classical simulations.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform is a viable candidate for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating many-body physics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and continuum limits that recover diffusion theory.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that treats both jump and diffusion processes on equal footing, enabling consistent analysis of pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying stochastic thermodynamics and nonequilibrium processes, but the paper is primarily mathematical and not directly focused on quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry reductions to accelerate classical simulation of Clifford-dominated quantum circuits by optimizing stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become costly for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the tractable regime by exploiting symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that decompose multiqubit unitaries into stabilizer components more efficiently, leveraging group-theoretic properties to reduce the number of terms.
result: The proposed methods enable optimal stabilizer decompositions for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits, significantly reducing the computational cost for circuits dominated by Clifford gates.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the verification of quantum advantage experiments.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to reduce space and time overhead, especially for small-angle rotations that are costly in standard schemes.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: The architecture yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms by optimizing error correction overhead.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma
abstract:

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Extends entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems using a colloidal monolayer Ising lattice, revealing exponential relation between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
motivation: To understand the universal relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation dynamics in disordered systems, extending known scaling laws to spin systems.
method: Experimental extraction of spin configurations from a buckled colloidal monolayer that mimics a 2D Ising lattice, measuring configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
result: Found a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time, analogous to the Adam-Gibbs relation in glass-forming liquids.
conclusion: The entropy scaling law is universal across different disordered systems, including spin systems, bridging the gap between spin physics and glass physics.

title: From Local Weight Selection To Zeno Slowdown In An Open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain With A Single Local Loss
authors: Y. T. Wang And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:

We study a quadratic open SSH chain with a single-site loss and show that the many-body fermionic Lindblad problem admits an exact reduction to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. Its rapidities generate the complete Liouvillian spectrum and reveal three mechan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012457] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Liouvillian spectrum of an open SSH chain with a single loss, revealing three mechanisms for Zeno slowdown.
motivation: Understanding how local dissipation affects topological systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The many-body Lindblad problem is reduced to a non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one impurity, whose rapidities yield the full Liouvillian spectrum.
result: Three mechanisms for Zeno slowdown are identified: topological edge state protection, band-edge van Hove singularity, and dark state formation.
conclusion: Local loss can induce Zeno slowdown via distinct mechanisms, with implications for controlling dissipation in quantum systems.

method: Integrates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture, leveraging cluster states and fault-tolerant protocols.
result: Substantial reduction in resource overhead compared to linear-optics-based architectures, with improved error thresholds.
conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Expander Quantum Low Density Parity Check Codes Against Long-range Correlated Errors In Memory

tldr: This paper studies the performance of expander quantum LDPC codes under long-range correlated errors in quantum memory, showing that such codes can achieve fault tolerance with constant space overhead against certain correlated noise models.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory typically assumes independent or local errors, but realistic noise can be long-range correlated. Understanding whether constant-overhead codes can handle such errors is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the error correction capability of expander quantum LDPC codes under a correlated error model using statistical mechanics mapping and numerical simulations, evaluating logical error rates and thresholds.
result: They find that expander quantum LDPC codes can tolerate long-range correlated errors with constant space overhead, provided the correlations decay sufficiently fast, and they derive conditions for fault tolerance.
conclusion: Expander quantum LDPC codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory even under non-local noise, but the results are specific to certain correlation regimes and may not extend to all practical scenarios.

result: The framework provides a systematic way to quantize the electromagnetic field in lossy cavities with position-dependent coupling, enabling accurate modeling of quantum optical phenomena.
conclusion: This work advances the theoretical toolkit for cavity quantum electrodynamics in lossy systems, relevant for hybrid quantum systems involving cavity-coupled emitters.

result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order in time for all three Dyson symmetry classes (orthogonal, unitary, symplectic).
conclusion: The results provide a detailed characterization of spectral correlations in chaotic quantum many-body systems, confirming universality classes.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.

result: They demonstrate that universal fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in 2D using this approach, avoiding the need for complex braiding operations.
conclusion: This work provides a new pathway toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation by simplifying the implementation of logical gates in 2D architectures.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order

result: Demonstrates that the proposed codes can correct errors in a single round of syndrome extraction for fermionic and chiral topological phases.

result: They demonstrate that constant qubit overhead and low time overhead are achievable with their scheme.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more practical.

result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to standard distillation methods, making it suitable for near-term quantum processors with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path to reduce resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi

tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel, pruning unlikely ones to balance accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding massive classical computation.
conclusion: Beam search decoding is a practical solution for quantum LDPC codes, enabling efficient error correction in near-term quantum computers.

method: Proposes twisted color circuits that enable non-Clifford gates on a planar 2D color code with nearest-neighbor couplings, using a just-in-time decoder for fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates scalable circuits that achieve fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates on a planar chip, reducing the overhead compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: The twisted color circuit approach provides a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures.

result: The proposed relation leads to a significant reduction in T-count compared to standard methods, improving the efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and measures of robustness and locality for Majorana bound states, accounting for interactions.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to evaluate whether a system hosts robust Majorana bound states suitable for braiding.
conclusion: The work offers a framework to guide experimental detection and utilization of Majorana bound states in quantum-dot setups.

title: Berry-phase-induced Canonical Structure Of Quantum Fluctuations Across The Mott-superfluid Phase Diagram
authors: Idan S. Wallerstein And Eytan Grosfeld

motivation: To provide a correct low-energy effective theory for the Bose-Hubbard model across the phase transition, addressing quantitative and fundamental failures of existing cumulant expansions.
method: Uses a field-theoretical approach incorporating Berry phase to derive a canonical structure for quantum fluctuations, likely via path integral or effective action methods.
result: Shows that cumulant expansions fail in the superfluid phase both quantitatively and fundamentally, and provides a unified description that captures the correct low-energy dynamics.
conclusion: The Berry-phase-induced canonical structure is essential for correctly describing quantum fluctuations across the Mott-superfluid transition, offering a more accurate theoretical framework.

authors: Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, And Eduardo Miranda

tldr: This paper solves a non-Hermitian disordered interacting fermion chain exactly, showing non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interactions, and non-Hermiticity in low-dimensional quantum systems.
method: Exact low-energy solution of the non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson chain with interactions using a mapping to a spin chain.
result: Non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy and eliminates its scaling, while spin susceptibilities diverge at finite temperature.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian hopping fundamentally alters entanglement properties, with implications for disordered quantum systems.

method: The authors derive a form of the local equilibrium density operator that is invariant under pseudogauge transformations by incorporating appropriate constraints.
result: They obtain an operator that remains unchanged under pseudogauge transformations, providing a consistent framework for relativistic thermodynamics.
conclusion: The proposed operator is suitable for modeling local equilibrium in relativistic systems, but the work is highly theoretical and specialized, with limited direct connection to the user's core interests in quantum thermodynamics or information processing.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on dynamics and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems, which may lead to new material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders like superconducting and magnetic phases.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the work is primarily a review of condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Three-dimensional sub-Doppler Cooling Of $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ In A Penning Trap

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review how maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques are used to model recorded electrical activity from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that theoretical principles from statistical physics can predict neural activity patterns.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Observation Of Sine-Gordon-Like Solitons In A Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Yannick Deller, Alexander Schmutz, Raphael Schäfer, Alexander Flamm, Florian Schmitt, Ido Siovitz, Thomas Gasenzer, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Helmut Strobel, And Markus K. Oberthaler
abstract:
Author(s): Yannick Deller, Alexander Schmutz, Raphael Schäfer, Alexander Flamm, Florian Schmitt, Ido Siovitz, Thomas Gasenzer, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Helmut Strobel, and Markus K. Oberthaler

We experimentally generate sine-Gordon-like solitons in a spin-1 spinor BEC utilizing a robust and reproducible local phase-imprinting scheme. We find that the soliton velocity can be tuned by the effective quadratic Zeeman shift. This enables the investigation of controlled soliton interactions, in…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053401] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of sine-Gordon-like solitons in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate with tunable velocity via quadratic Zeeman shift.
motivation: To experimentally generate and control sine-Gordon solitons in a spinor BEC, enabling study of soliton interactions and dynamics.
method: A local phase-imprinting scheme is used to create solitons in a spin-1 BEC, with velocity controlled by the effective quadratic Zeeman shift.
result: Soliton velocity is tunable, and controlled soliton interactions are demonstrated.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for studying nonlinear excitations in quantum fluids, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Constant-Amplitude $2π$ Phase Modulation From Topological Pole-Zero Winding
authors: Alex Krasnok
abstract:
Author(s): Alex Krasnok

A resonant phase shifter should rotate a complex optical field without changing its magnitude, but loss and coupling usually make resonant phase tuning change the intensity as well. We introduce a pole-zero synthesis rule that produces a full [MATH] phase winding at a chosen scattering magnitude for a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053801] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a topological pole-zero winding method to achieve constant-amplitude 2π phase modulation in resonant optical systems.
motivation: Resonant phase shifters typically suffer from intensity variation during phase tuning; the authors aim to achieve pure phase modulation without amplitude change.
method: The authors introduce a pole-zero synthesis rule that exploits topological winding in the complex frequency plane to produce a full 2π phase shift at a constant scattering magnitude.
result: They demonstrate theoretically that the proposed rule yields a constant-amplitude 2π phase modulation, overcoming the usual loss and coupling limitations.
conclusion: The work provides a new approach for designing resonant phase shifters with ideal phase-only modulation, relevant for photonic applications.

title: $D$-Wave Phonon Angular Momentum Texture In Altermagnets By Magnon-Phonon Hybridization
authors: Hannah Bendin, Alexander Mook, Ingrid Mertig, And Robin R. Neumann
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Bendin, Alexander Mook, Ingrid Mertig, and Robin R. Neumann

In altermagnets, the magnon bands are anisotropically spin split in reciprocal space without relativistic or dipolar spin-spin interactions. In this Letter, we theoretically study magnons and phonons coupled by spin-lattice interaction in a two-dimensional square-lattice [MATH]-wave altermagnet. We sho…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056701] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon-phonon hybridization in altermagnets, revealing a d-wave phonon angular momentum texture.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit anisotropic magnon spin splitting without relativistic interactions; coupling to phonons via spin-lattice interaction may create novel hybrid excitations.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-dimensional square-lattice d-wave altermagnet, computing magnon and phonon spectra and their hybridization due to spin-lattice coupling.
result: They find that magnon-phonon hybridization induces a d-wave texture in the phonon angular momentum, which can be detected experimentally.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for generating phonon angular momentum textures, relevant for spintronics and magnonics.

title: Non-Abelian Electric Field And Zitterbewegung On A Photonic Frequency Chain
authors: Shu Yang (杨树), Bengy Tsz Tsun Wong (黄梓峻), Jinbing Hu (胡金兵), And Yi Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Shu Yang (杨树), Bengy Tsz Tsun Wong (黄梓峻), Jinbing Hu (胡金兵), and Yi Yang (杨易)

A ring of optical fiber can be made to host phenomena that originated in the realm of high-energy physics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056901] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates non-Abelian electric fields and Zitterbewegung on a photonic frequency chain using a ring of optical fiber.
motivation: To simulate high-energy physics phenomena in a classical photonic platform, exploring non-Abelian gauge fields and relativistic electron dynamics.
method: The authors construct a synthetic frequency dimension in a fiber ring with modulated couplings, realizing a non-Abelian electric field and observing Zitterbewegung.
result: They observe signatures of non-Abelian electric fields and Zitterbewegung, confirming the simulation of relativistic quantum effects.
conclusion: The work provides a classical photonic analog of non-Abelian gauge theories and relativistic quantum mechanics, with potential for studying topological phenomena.

title: Intrinsic Nernst Effect From Berry Curvature In Superconductors
authors: Tzu-Chi Hsieh, Cong Xiao, And Yi-Ting Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Tzu-Chi Hsieh, Cong Xiao, and Yi-Ting Hsu

The Nernst effect acts as direct probe of Berry curvature to test topological superconductivity in 2D material with spin-orbit coupling.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046002] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the intrinsic Nernst effect from Berry curvature in superconductors, focusing on topological superconductivity in 2D materials.
motivation: To probe topological superconductivity using the Nernst effect as a direct measure of Berry curvature.
method: Theoretical analysis of Berry curvature contributions to the Nernst effect in 2D superconductors with spin-orbit coupling.
result: The intrinsic Nernst effect is shown to be a direct probe of Berry curvature, enabling detection of topological superconductivity.
conclusion: The Nernst effect can serve as an experimental tool to test topological superconductivity in 2D materials.

title: Anyon Dispersion From Nonuniform Magnetic Field On The Sphere
authors: Mina-Lou Schleith, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), And Eslam Khalaf
abstract:
Author(s): Mina-Lou Schleith, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), and Eslam Khalaf

The discovery of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré systems has raised the possibility of realizing phases of itinerant anyons, whose mobility requires the absence of continuous magnetic translation symmetry (CMTS). Motivated by this, we consider anyons on the sphere in the presence o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046506] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anyon dispersion on a sphere under a nonuniform magnetic field, motivated by fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré systems.
motivation: The discovery of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré systems raises the possibility of realizing phases of itinerant anyons, whose mobility requires the absence of continuous magnetic translation symmetry.
method: The authors consider anyons on a sphere in the presence of a nonuniform magnetic field and analyze their dispersion.
result: The paper presents a theoretical analysis of anyon dispersion under these conditions.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding anyon mobility in moiré systems, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Experimental Realization Of Synthetic Magnonic Lattice Via Floquet Engineering
authors: Amin Pishehvar, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Zhaoyou Wang, Zixin Yan, Yu Jiang, Liang Jiang, Benedetta Flebus, And Xufeng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Amin Pishehvar, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Zhaoyou Wang, Zixin Yan, Yu Jiang, Liang Jiang, Benedetta Flebus, and Xufeng Zhang

Magnonic systems, which exploit spin-wave excitations in magnetic materials, offer a promising platform for coherent information processing due to their low dissipation, strong nonlinearities, and intrinsic nonreciprocity. However, scaling magnonic circuits remains challenging, particularly with low…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046706] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes a synthetic magnonic lattice using Floquet engineering, demonstrating coherent spin-wave dynamics in a periodically driven magnetic system.
motivation: Scaling magnonic circuits for coherent information processing is challenging; synthetic lattices offer a way to engineer complex magnonic band structures.
method: The authors use Floquet engineering with spatially modulated microwave fields to create a synthetic lattice for magnons in a yttrium iron garnet film, and probe the band structure via Brillouin light scattering.
result: They observe Floquet-induced band gaps and topological edge states, confirming the synthetic lattice formation and coherent control of magnon dynamics.
conclusion: Synthetic magnonic lattices via Floquet engineering provide a new platform for studying topological phases and coherent information processing in magnonic systems.

title: Observation Of Radiation-Loss-Based Non-Hermitian Point Gap In Photonic Crystals
authors: Yuto Moritake, Nozomi Ogawa, Issei Takeda, Yusuke Ohinata, Takahiro Uemura, Taiki Yoda, Kenta Takata, Eiichi Kuramochi, Hisashi Sumikura, And Masaya Notomi
abstract:
Author(s): Yuto Moritake, Nozomi Ogawa, Issei Takeda, Yusuke Ohinata, Takahiro Uemura, Taiki Yoda, Kenta Takata, Eiichi Kuramochi, Hisashi Sumikura, and Masaya Notomi

A non-Hermitian point gap (NHPG) is a unique phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems and induces a non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). In photonic crystals, NHPG and NHSE have previously been explored mainly through material loss, where the typically low [MATH] factors make direct observation of complex freq…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046903] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes a non-Hermitian point gap in photonic crystals using radiation loss, demonstrating the non-Hermitian skin effect.
motivation: Non-Hermitian point gaps and the associated skin effect have been studied mainly with material loss, but direct observation of complex frequency dispersion in photonic crystals has been challenging due to low Q factors.
method: The authors use radiation loss instead of material loss in photonic crystals to achieve a non-Hermitian point gap, and perform experimental measurements to observe the complex frequency dispersion.
result: They successfully observe the non-Hermitian point gap and the non-Hermitian skin effect in photonic crystals via radiation loss.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for studying non-Hermitian phenomena in photonic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Flux Magnetism In A Strongly Interacting Dipolar Lattice Supersolid Under Tunable Gauge Fields
authors: Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, And Luca Barbiero
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, and Luca Barbiero

Supersolidity and magnetism are fundamental phenomena characterizing strongly correlated matter. Here we unveil a mechanism that directly connects these two regimes and can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems. Specifically, we exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux magnetism in a dipolar lattice supersolid under tunable gauge fields, connecting supersolidity and magnetism in ultracold atomic systems.
motivation: To unveil a mechanism directly connecting supersolidity and magnetism, which are fundamental phenomena in strongly correlated matter, and to demonstrate experimental accessibility in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthanide atoms to realize a dipolar lattice supersolid and apply tunable gauge fields to induce flux magnetism.
result: They observe a novel magnetic phase arising from the interplay of supersolid order and gauge fields, characterized by spontaneous magnetization and topological features.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between supersolidity and magnetism, opening new avenues for exploring strongly correlated quantum matter with ultracold atoms.

title: Interaction Of Strong Electromagnetic Waves With Unmagnetized Pair Plasmas
authors: Navin Sridhar, Emanuele Sobacchi, Lorenzo Sironi, Masanori Iwamoto, Daniel Grošelj, And Brandon K. Russell
abstract:
Author(s): Navin Sridhar, Emanuele Sobacchi, Lorenzo Sironi, Masanori Iwamoto, Daniel Grošelj, and Brandon K. Russell

We investigate analytically and numerically the interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with unmagnetized pair plasmas. We show that the interaction is governed by a single nonlinearity parameter, [MATH], defined as the ratio of the wave strength parameter to the wave frequency in un…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 045102] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with unmagnetized pair plasmas, focusing on nonlinear plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the nonlinear interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with pair plasmas is important for astrophysical and laboratory plasma physics.
method: The authors use analytical theory and numerical simulations to characterize the interaction, identifying a single nonlinearity parameter that governs the dynamics.
result: They show that the interaction is governed by a single parameter and provide analytical and numerical results for various regimes.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonlinear wave-plasma interactions in pair plasmas, with implications for astrophysical environments.

title: Hidden Dissipation In Topological Insulators: Near-field Radiation From Local Shot Noise
authors: Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, and Jian Wang

Finite-frequency local shot noise acting as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors reveals a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy rather than conventional transport measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046303] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiation from local shot noise in topological insulators as a hidden dissipation channel.
motivation: Understanding energy dissipation in topological insulators is important for applications, but conventional transport measurements miss certain loss channels.
method: The authors theoretically analyze finite-frequency local shot noise as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors.
result: They identify a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy.
conclusion: Near-field radiation from shot noise provides a new way to probe dissipation in topological insulators beyond standard transport.

title: Finite-Momentum Pairing And Superlattice Superconductivity In Valley-Imbalanced Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, and Mathias S. Scheurer

Superconducting instabilities in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral tetralayer graphene reveal the formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.

tldr: This paper studies finite-momentum pairing and superlattice superconductivity in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding superconducting instabilities in graphene systems with valley imbalance is important for condensed matter physics, but does not directly relate to the user's research interests.
method: The authors theoretically analyze superconducting instabilities in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with valley imbalance, likely using mean-field theory or similar techniques.
result: They find formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of graphene-based superconductors but lacks connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unconventional Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals: A Hyperspatial Projective Construction
authors: Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Altermagnetism, a novel magnetic phase characterized by symmetry-protected, momentum-dependent spin splitting and collinear compensated magnetic moments, has thus far been explored primarily in periodic crystals. In this Letter, we extend the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals—aperiodic syst…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046704] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals using a hyperspatial projective construction.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied only in periodic crystals; this work explores its existence in aperiodic quasicrystals.
method: The authors use a hyperspatial projective construction to model altermagnetism in quasicrystals.
result: They demonstrate symmetry-protected spin splitting in quasicrystals, showing altermagnetism is not limited to periodic systems.
conclusion: Altermagnetism can exist in quasicrystals, broadening the scope of magnetic phases in aperiodic materials.

title: Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals
authors: Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, and Dong-Hui Xu

Altermagnets are a recently discovered class of magnetic materials that combine a collinear, zero-magnetization spin structure, characteristic of antiferromagnets, with spin-split electronic bands, a hallmark of ferromagnets. This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046705] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied in periodic crystals; this work extends the concept to quasicrystals, which lack translational symmetry.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling and analyze the electronic structure and spin polarization via symmetry arguments and numerical calculations.
result: They find that quasicrystals can host altermagnetic order with spin-split bands, despite the absence of periodic order.
conclusion: Quasicrystals provide a new platform for altermagnetism, expanding the material landscape for spintronics.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard model using numerical techniques.
result: They find magnetic correlations and possibly novel phases in the doped triangular lattice.
conclusion: The work provides insights into SU(3) magnetism but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Displacive Quantum Critical Point In Superconducting Hydrides: The Case Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{3}\mathrm{S}$
authors: Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, And Michele Casula
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, and Michele Casula

[MATH] sulfur hydride has been widely investigated for its high superconducting critical temperature [MATH] of 203 K at about [MATH]. Despite being the precursor of superconducting hydrides, a detailed picture of its structural phase diagra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046102] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a displacive quantum critical point in superconducting H3S, focusing on structural phase transitions and their impact on superconductivity.
motivation: Understanding the structural phase diagram of H3S is crucial for explaining its high superconducting critical temperature and for designing better hydride superconductors.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and anharmonic phonon theory to study the pressure-temperature phase diagram of H3S, identifying a quantum critical point associated with a displacive phase transition.
result: They find a quantum critical point at around 150 GPa and 100 K, where the structural transition between the cubic and tetragonal phases becomes continuous, influencing the superconducting properties.
conclusion: The displacive quantum critical point may play a key role in the high-temperature superconductivity of H3S, suggesting that quantum critical fluctuations enhance the superconducting transition temperature.

title: Linear-combination-of-unitaries Decomposition For The Laplace Operator
authors: Thomas Hogancamp, Reuben Demirdjian, And Daniel Gunlycke
abstract:

We provide alternative linear-combination-of-unitaries decompositions for a class of discrete elliptic differential operators. Specifically, Poisson problems augmented with periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, and mixed boundary conditions are considered on the unit interval and on higher-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012455] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents linear-combination-of-unitaries decompositions for discrete elliptic differential operators, focusing on numerical methods for solving Poisson problems.
motivation: Efficient quantum algorithms for solving differential equations are needed, and the Laplace operator is a fundamental component in many PDEs.
method: The authors provide explicit LCU decompositions for the discrete Laplace operator under various boundary conditions, enabling Hamiltonian simulation or linear system solving.
result: Alternative LCU decompositions are derived that may reduce circuit depth or improve scalability for quantum solvers.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum numerical methods but does not directly address the user's core research directions in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Walks On A Defective Lattice: Boosting The Spreading Of Delocalized States Through Parrondo's Strategy
authors: João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, And Edgard P. M. Amorim

We investigate the quantum transport of delocalized states in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on a one-dimensional lattice containing a single defect. The defect is modeled by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to the edges that connect the site corresponding to the mean position of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012459] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time quantum walks on a defective lattice and uses Parrondo's strategy to enhance the spreading of delocalized states.
motivation: Understanding quantum transport in disordered systems is important for quantum information processing, but the paper focuses on a specific transport phenomenon rather than core quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect using complex-valued hopping amplitudes and apply Parrondo's strategy to boost the spreading of delocalized states.
result: They find that the Parrondo strategy can enhance the spreading of delocalized states in the presence of a defect.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum transport but does not directly advance the user's core research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Limitations Of Entangled Two-photon Absorption Detection
authors: R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, And B. Brecht
abstract:
Author(s): R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, and B. Brecht

We introduce a method for determining the sensitivity of any given entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) measurement. By modeling all signal and noise contributions to the measurement, we derive a single numerical value that describes the sensitivity of the ETPA measurement in Göppert-Mayer units. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013718] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the sensitivity limits of entangled two-photon absorption measurements, providing a method to quantify detection sensitivity in Göppert-Mayer units.
motivation: Entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) is a promising technique for spectroscopy and sensing, but its practical sensitivity is limited by noise and experimental constraints. A systematic method to evaluate and compare ETPA measurements is needed.
method: The authors model all signal and noise contributions in an ETPA measurement and derive a single numerical figure of merit (in Göppert-Mayer units) that quantifies the measurement sensitivity.
result: They identify fundamental limitations due to photon statistics, detector noise, and background, and show that current ETPA experiments operate far from the fundamental sensitivity bound.
conclusion: The proposed sensitivity metric enables fair comparison of different ETPA implementations and highlights the gap between current performance and theoretical limits, guiding future improvements.

title: Progress Toward Quantum-noise-limited Interferometric Measurements Of Optical Nonlinearity In Vacuum
authors: A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, And M. Pittman
abstract:

Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum must behave as a nonlinear optical medium: The vacuum optical index should increase when it is stressed by intense electromagnetic fields. The Deflection of Light by Light project aims to measure it by using intense and ultrashort laser pulses. The ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013519] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports progress toward measuring the quantum vacuum's nonlinear optical response using intense laser pulses.
motivation: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium, but this effect has not been directly observed. The authors aim to measure it via interferometric techniques.
method: The experiment uses intense ultrashort laser pulses and a high-sensitivity interferometric setup to detect the predicted deflection of light by light in vacuum.
result: The paper describes the experimental apparatus and preliminary results, showing progress toward achieving quantum-noise-limited sensitivity.
conclusion: The work advances the experimental capability to probe vacuum nonlinearity, but does not yet provide a definitive measurement.

title: Quantum-to-semiclassical Husimi Dynamics Of non-Hermitian Localization Transitions
authors: Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, And Ranjan Modak
abstract:
Author(s): Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, and Ranjan Modak

The localization transition in the Hermitian Aubry-André model is known to have a classical origin, with the critical point being exactly predictable from an analysis of classical phase-space trajectories. Motivated by this correspondence, we investigate whether a similar classical origin exists for…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013318] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies localization transitions in a non-Hermitian Aubry-André model using Husimi dynamics, finding a classical origin for the transition.
motivation: To understand whether the localization transition in non-Hermitian systems has a classical origin, similar to the Hermitian Aubry-André model.
method: The authors analyze classical phase-space trajectories and Husimi distributions to characterize the localization transition in a non-Hermitian variant of the Aubry-André model.
result: They find that the critical point of the non-Hermitian localization transition can be predicted from classical dynamics, analogous to the Hermitian case.
conclusion: The localization transition in this non-Hermitian model has a classical origin, extending the correspondence between classical and quantum dynamics to non-Hermitian systems.

title: Optimization Of Two-photon Excitation By Indistinguishable Photons In A Three-level Atom
authors: Masood Valipour, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Karolina Słowik, And Anita Dąbrowska

We investigate the excitation of a three-level ladder-type atom by a unidirectional field with a pair of indistinguishable photons. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 013717] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes two-photon excitation in a three-level atom using indistinguishable photons.
motivation: To understand and maximize the excitation probability of the upper atomic state via two-photon absorption with quantum light.
method: Analytical derivation of two-photon absorption probability and optimization of the two-photon state.
result: Determined the optimal two-photon state that maximizes upper state population.
conclusion: The work provides insights into light-matter interaction with quantum light, but is not directly relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Entangled Two-photon Absorption In Cesium Atoms And The Limitations Of The Far-off-resonance Approximation
authors: Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, And Mayerlin Nuñez Portela
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, and Mayerlin Nuñez Portela

The discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in the process of entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood. Atomic systems are a promising alternative for investigating this process without the systematic effects present in molecules. We present a theoretical st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013120] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, focusing on limitations of the far-off-resonance approximation.
motivation: Discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in entangled two-photon absorption are not fully understood; atomic systems offer a cleaner testbed than molecules.
method: A theoretical study of entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, analyzing the far-off-resonance approximation and its limitations.
result: The far-off-resonance approximation is found to be inadequate for describing entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms under certain conditions.
conclusion: Atomic systems can help resolve discrepancies, but improved theoretical models beyond the far-off-resonance approximation are needed.

title: Control Of Ion-photoelectron Entanglement In Rabi Oscillations By Time-delayed Pulses
authors: Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, And Yueming Zhou
abstract:

We investigate theoretically the coherent dynamics of helium photoionization driven by a pair of time-delayed laser pulses using the [MATH]-dimensional two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Our numerical calculations reveal that the resulting photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly d…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ion-photoelectron entanglement in Rabi oscillations driven by time-delayed laser pulses in helium photoionization.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement dynamics in photoionization processes, which is relevant to attosecond science and quantum control.
method: Numerical solution of the two-dimensional two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation for helium driven by a pair of time-delayed laser pulses.
result: Photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly doublet structures, indicating entanglement between the ion and photoelectron that can be controlled via pulse delay.
conclusion: Time-delayed pulses provide a means to control ion-photoelectron entanglement, with potential applications in quantum information and attosecond physics.

title: Mesoscopic Scattering Dynamics Under Generic Uniform Su(2) Gauge Fields: Spin-momentum Relaxation And Coherent Backscattering
authors: Masataka Kakoi, Christian Miniatura, And Keith Slevin
