Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates under strain and doping.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films with varying strain and doping levels.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity in these nickelates, constraining theoretical models.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring and modeling physical systems using large language models.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery, enabling the uncovering of underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and models physical systems.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate scientific modeling, but the paper focuses on AI methodology rather than advancing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation below the mode coupling temperature.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe dynamic properties.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism driving relaxation in this regime.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems at deep supercooling.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, focusing on their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and detection via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the nonperturbative quantization of chiral solitons and their role as low-energy excitations in ferromagnetic spin chains.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral solitons and suggests experimental verification through neutron scattering.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop non-perturbative methods for studying conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and operator content.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs and compute scaling dimensions of primary operators.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, revealing emergent supersymmetry and enabling further exploration of strongly coupled theories.

authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.

result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, relevant to spintronics.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for engineering robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin

conclusion: This work identifies a new class of materials with robust flat bands at room temperature, which could enable studies of strongly correlated physics without cryogenic constraints.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its approximation is classically hard, motivating a quantum algorithmic approach.

result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and demonstrating the algorithm's feasibility.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial approximation as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, including nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The authors review the history of the field, propose a definition, and survey recent topics such as nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
result: A definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems is offered, and recent developments are summarized.
conclusion: Active matter is a distinct field within nonequilibrium physics, with emerging connections to quantum systems.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Quantum linear system solvers are a fundamental subroutine in many quantum algorithms, and a structured review is needed to organize the rapidly growing literature.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, compares their query complexities, and discusses applications in machine learning, differential equations, and quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements; future work should focus on near-term implementations and error mitigation.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism since its experimental realization in 2016.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights new phenomena such as topological magnetic phases, nonequilibrium dynamics, and Floquet effects in 2D magnets.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, expanding theoretical understanding and opening new directions for applications in spintronics and beyond.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects.
conclusion: Kagome metals host a rich variety of exotic states due to frustration and interference, but the paper is primarily a materials science review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents under a single field-theoretic framework.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in reaction-diffusion processes.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unified tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to be a rich field with broad applications, and interdisciplinary collaboration remains essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a paradigmatic example of frustrated magnetism.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental studies on candidate materials.
result: Highlights key candidate materials and their topological properties such as chiral edge modes.
conclusion: The review offers essential insights for researchers working on quantum spin liquids.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored. This review aims to consolidate quantum-mechanical understanding.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, providing a comprehensive overview.
result: It highlights quantum effects such as tunneling, superposition, and entanglement in skyrmions, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities, but further research is needed to harness them for practical quantum technologies.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, probing dark matter and fundamental symmetries.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy through spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons.
method: Review of theoretical models and experimental techniques for detecting spin-dependent interactions.
result: Summarizes current constraints and future prospects for various exotic spin-dependent interactions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential to reveal new physics beyond the standard model.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from assumptions not being met.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how these can be exploited.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to exceed classical bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, opening avenues for novel material properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in various quantum platforms.
result: Summarizes progress in synthetic quantum matter in exotic geometries, highlighting connections to topology and cosmology.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics beyond standard geometries.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments, and proposes a unified mathematical and conceptual framework for self-alignment.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with broad implications for applications.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, exploring whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement between massive particles.
result: Ongoing experiments aim to determine whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement, guiding future theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems serve as interfaces to probe quantum gravity effects, but conclusive results are pending.

title: Mode Conservation And Conversion In Polyatomic Phononic Crystals With Temporal Interfaces
authors: Mahmoud M. Samak And Osama R. Bilal
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud M. Samak and Osama R. Bilal

A sudden change in material properties creates a temporal interface and forces a propagating wave to change its frequency while preserving its wave number. In contrast to monoatomic lattices with a single-frequency–wave-number pair, polyatomic lattices support multiple frequencies for each wave numb…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056601] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mode conservation and conversion in polyatomic phononic crystals with temporal interfaces, focusing on classical wave propagation in mechanical lattices.
motivation: Understanding how waves behave when material properties change suddenly is important for controlling wave propagation in phononic crystals.
method: The authors analyze polyatomic lattices with temporal interfaces, deriving conditions for mode conservation and conversion based on frequency and wave number matching.
result: They find that polyatomic lattices support multiple frequency-wave-number pairs, leading to mode conversion at temporal interfaces, unlike monoatomic lattices.
conclusion: The work provides insights into wave dynamics in time-varying phononic crystals, with potential applications in wave filtering and energy harvesting.

title: Polaron-Driven Switching Of Octupolar Order In Doped $5{\mathrm{d}}^{2}$ Double Perovskite
authors: Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, and Cesare Franchini

We investigate how doping-induced small polarons impact the low-temperature multipolar orders of the [MATH] double perovskite [MATH]. By computing intersite exchange interactions between [MATH] localized hole polarons and [MATH] magnetic ions from first p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046504] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-driven switching of octupolar order in a doped double perovskite, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how doping-induced small polarons affect low-temperature multipolar orders in a specific material.
method: First-principles calculations of intersite exchange interactions between hole polarons and magnetic ions.
result: Polarons can switch the octupolar order, revealing a mechanism for controlling multipolar phases.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into polaron-magnetism coupling in double perovskites, but are not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Orbital-spin Conversion In Solid High-order Harmonic Generation By Ring Configurations
authors: Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, And Jianghua Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, and Jianghua Luo

We theoretically investigate the interaction between azimuthal vector vortex beams and a segmented ring medium, revealing orbital-to-spin conversion in strong-field high-order harmonic generation. We show that engineered gaps in the ring target break the light-matter symmetry and mediate the transfe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013122] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital-to-spin conversion in high-order harmonic generation using vector vortex beams and segmented ring targets.
motivation: To understand and control the transfer of orbital angular momentum to spin angular momentum in strong-field light-matter interactions.
method: Theoretical investigation using azimuthal vector vortex beams interacting with a segmented ring medium, with engineered gaps to break symmetry.
result: Orbital-to-spin conversion is observed in high-order harmonic generation, mediated by the broken symmetry from the gaps.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for angular momentum conversion in nonlinear optics, with potential applications in ultrafast optics and light-matter control.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, and Agustin Palacios-Laloy

We report a comprehensive characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam [MATH]-based vector optically pumped magnetometer, and identify its main origins. In its optimal regime, the sensor provided vector magnetic readings with noise below $30{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012619] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the intrinsic noise of a zero-field metastable helium-4 optically pumped magnetometer.
motivation: Understanding the origins of noise in optically pumped magnetometers is important for improving their sensitivity, but the paper focuses on a specific sensor technology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental characterization of the noise sources in a single-beam vector magnetometer based on metastable helium-4.
result: They identify the main noise origins and achieve vector magnetic readings with noise below 300 fT/Hz^{1/2} in the optimal regime.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the noise mechanisms of this type of magnetometer, which may aid in sensor optimization.

title: Calculating Resonance Using Parametric Equations Of Motion In The Limit Of The Complex Absorbing Potential Strength Parameter ($η→{0}^{+}$)
authors: Deepak Kumar And Ashish Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Kumar and Ashish Kumar Gupta

Since complex absorbing potentials (CAPs) are nonphysical in nature, they can introduce artificial perturbations into the system, which may lead to shifts in the calculated energy. This study presents a methodology to eliminate artificial reflections caused by the CAP using a backward parametric equ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012818] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to eliminate artificial reflections from complex absorbing potentials in resonance calculations using parametric equations of motion.
motivation: Complex absorbing potentials introduce artificial perturbations that shift calculated energies; the authors aim to correct these shifts.
method: A backward parametric equation of motion is used in the limit of the CAP strength parameter approaching zero to remove artificial reflections.
result: The methodology successfully eliminates artificial reflections, yielding more accurate resonance energies.
conclusion: The proposed approach improves the accuracy of resonance calculations by mitigating CAP-induced artifacts.

title: Wetting Of Quantum Fluids: A Route To Free-standing Shell-shaped Quantum Droplets
authors: Francesco Ancilotto
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Ancilotto

We investigate wetting phenomena between self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture of [MATH], and [MATH] atoms. Within a density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections, we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013317] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wetting phenomena in quantum fluid droplets using density-functional theory.
motivation: To understand the wetting behavior of self-bound quantum fluids and the formation of free-standing shell-shaped droplets.
method: A density-functional approach with mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections is used to model a three-component Bose mixture.
result: The analysis reveals conditions under which wetting and shell-shaped droplet formation occur.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum fluid wetting but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dichotomous Effect Of Oxygen Vacancy In High-entropy Oxide Films With Mott Electrons
authors: Suresh Chandra Joshi, Nandana Bhattacharya, Ke Qu, Manav Beniwal, Haonan Wang, Jyotirmay Maity, Prithwijit Mandal, Hua Zhou, Zhenzhong Yang, Christoph Klewe, And Srimanta Middey
abstract:
Author(s): Suresh Chandra Joshi, Nandana Bhattacharya, Ke Qu, Manav Beniwal, Haonan Wang, Jyotirmay Maity, Prithwijit Mandal, Hua Zhou, Zhenzhong Yang, Christoph Klewe, and Srimanta Middey

Contrary to traditional approaches, high entropy oxides (HEOs) strategically employ cationic disorder to engineer tunable functionalities. This disorder, stemming from multiple elements at the same crystallographic site, disrupts local symmetry and induces local distortions. By investigating a serie…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024209] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of oxygen vacancies on the electronic properties of high-entropy oxide films with Mott electrons.
motivation: To understand how oxygen vacancies influence the functionality of high-entropy oxides, which are promising for tunable electronic properties.
method: The authors investigate a series of high-entropy oxide films, analyzing the role of oxygen vacancies through experimental characterization and theoretical modeling.
result: Oxygen vacancies have a dichotomous effect, either enhancing or degrading electronic properties depending on their concentration and distribution.
conclusion: Controlling oxygen vacancies is crucial for optimizing the performance of high-entropy oxide devices.

title: Enhanced Superconductivity In Atomically Thin Noble Metals: From Quantum Confinement To Interface-induced Lifshitz Transition
authors: Chun-Jie Zhang, Bing Zhang, Yapeng Wu, Xiao-Ping Li, And Lei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Jie Zhang, Bing Zhang, Yapeng Wu, Xiao-Ping Li, and Lei Wang

Unlocking superconductivity in the intrinsically nonsuperconducting noble metals Au, Ag, and Cu represents a fundamental challenge in low-dimensional quantum materials. While quantum confinement in the atomically thin limit is known to trigger emergent superconductivity, strategies to amplify this m…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024514] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies enhanced superconductivity in atomically thin noble metals via quantum confinement and interface-induced Lifshitz transition.
motivation: To understand and amplify emergent superconductivity in intrinsically nonsuperconducting noble metals (Au, Ag, Cu) in the atomically thin limit.
method: Theoretical analysis using first-principles calculations or model Hamiltonians to study quantum confinement effects and electronic structure changes.
result: Identifies mechanisms for enhanced superconductivity, likely involving increased density of states or modified electron-phonon coupling.
conclusion: Quantum confinement and interface effects can significantly enhance superconductivity in thin noble metal films.

title: Real-time Exciton Dynamics In Two-dimensional Materials Under Ultrashort Laser Pulses
authors: Dmitry Tumakov And Daria Popova-Gorelova
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitry Tumakov and Daria Popova-Gorelova

The optical response of two-dimensional materials is often significantly impacted by excitonic effects due to the reduced screening of attractive Coulomb interactions in low-dimensional systems. Accurate modeling of exciton formation and real-time dynamics is essential to understanding their ultrafa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045127] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies real-time exciton dynamics in two-dimensional materials under ultrashort laser pulses using time-dependent density functional theory.
motivation: Understanding exciton formation and dynamics is crucial for interpreting ultrafast optical experiments in low-dimensional materials.
method: The authors employ real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) to simulate the electron dynamics and exciton formation in monolayer MoS2 and other 2D materials.
result: They observe the formation of excitons and their coherent oscillation, and analyze the effect of laser pulse parameters on the exciton dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into ultrafast exciton dynamics, which is important for optoelectronic applications of 2D materials.

title: Interplay Of Disorder, Interlayer Coupling, And Hopping Transport In Sliding Ferroelectric Misfit ${(\text{PbS})}_{1.11}{\mathrm{VS}}_{2}$
authors: Jiří Volný, Cinthia Antunes Corrêa, Soňa Cádrová, Karel Výborný, Tim Verhagen, And Klára Uhlířová
abstract:
Author(s): Jiří Volný, Cinthia Antunes Corrêa, Soňa Cádrová, Karel Výborný, Tim Verhagen, and Klára Uhlířová

The misfit layered compound [MATH] shows a complex interplay of structural modulation, disorder, and charge dynamics that leads to unconventional magnetic and transport properties. High resolution scanning transmission microscopy and temperature-dependent single cry…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045431] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies structural modulation, disorder, and charge dynamics in a misfit layered compound, focusing on magnetic and transport properties.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interlayer coupling, and hopping transport in sliding ferroelectric misfit compounds.
method: High-resolution scanning transmission microscopy and temperature-dependent single-crystal transport measurements.
result: Reveals complex interplay leading to unconventional magnetic and transport properties.
conclusion: The compound exhibits rich physics due to structural modulation and disorder, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pressure-induced Redistribution Of Oxygen Hole States In ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10}$
authors: Guiwen Jiang, Liang Si, George A. Sawatzky, And Mi Jiang

Using density functional calculations and multiorbital, multiatom cluster exact diagonalization that includes local exchange and Coulomb interactions, we explored the local low-energy electronic states of trilayer [MATH] via a minimal ${}_{3}…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055130] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of La4Ni3O10 under pressure using DFT and cluster exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the pressure-induced redistribution of oxygen hole states in trilayer nickelates.
method: Density functional calculations combined with multiorbital, multiatom cluster exact diagonalization including local exchange and Coulomb interactions.
result: The local low-energy electronic states are explored, revealing how oxygen hole states redistribute under pressure.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the electronic properties of La4Ni3O10 under pressure, relevant to condensed matter physics.

title: Nonvolatile Control Of Half-metallicity In $A$-type Antiferromagnetic Bilayer $\mathrm{NiB}{\mathrm{r}}_{2}$
authors: Shasha Li, Chang Liu, Jingxin Xue, Ping Liu, Feng Li, And Yong Pu
abstract:

The electronic and magnetic properties of two-dimensional [MATH] bilayer are systematically investigated using first-principles calculations. We find that the metastable antialigned stacking [MATH] bilayer exhibits sliding ferroelectricity, where rever…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065426] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of electronic and magnetic properties of NiBr2 bilayer, focusing on sliding ferroelectricity and half-metallicity control.
motivation: To explore the electronic and magnetic properties of two-dimensional NiBr2 bilayer and investigate the possibility of controlling half-metallicity via nonvolatile means.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to compute electronic structure and magnetic properties of NiBr2 bilayer with different stacking configurations.
result: The metastable antialigned stacking exhibits sliding ferroelectricity, and reversal of electric polarization can control half-metallicity.
conclusion: The NiBr2 bilayer offers a platform for nonvolatile control of half-metallicity, relevant for spintronic applications.

title: Singularly Isostatic And Geometrically Unstable Rigidity Of Metal-organic Frameworks
authors: Christopher M. Owen And Michael J. Lawler
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher M. Owen and Michael J. Lawler

Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) combine high porosity with structural fragility, raising important questions about their mechanical stability. We develop a rigidity-based formalism in which spring networks parameterized by universal force field for metal-organic frameworks are used to construct rigi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014317] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the mechanical rigidity of metal-organic frameworks using a spring network model, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Metal-organic frameworks combine high porosity with structural fragility, motivating a study of their mechanical stability.
method: A rigidity-based formalism is developed using spring networks parameterized by a universal force field for metal-organic frameworks.
result: The analysis identifies singularly isostatic and geometrically unstable rigidity regimes.
conclusion: The formalism provides insight into the mechanical stability of MOFs but does not relate to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ratchet Effect Of Magnetic Skyrmions Modified By Anisotropy Of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
authors: Fanglin Meng, Linjie Liu, Weijin Chen, And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Fanglin Meng, Linjie Liu, Weijin Chen, and Yue Zheng

The directional transport of magnetic skyrmions under microwave magnetic fields, known as the skyrmion ratchet effect, offers a promising approach for driving skyrmions in materials with poor electrical conductivity. While ratchet effects affected by disorders, biharmonic magnetic fields, and biased…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024421] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ratchet effect of magnetic skyrmions under microwave fields, focusing on the influence of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy.
motivation: To understand and control skyrmion transport in materials with poor electrical conductivity, which is relevant for spintronic devices.
method: Micromagnetic simulations are used to model skyrmion dynamics under microwave magnetic fields with varying Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy.
result: The anisotropy of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction significantly modifies the skyrmion ratchet effect, affecting the direction and efficiency of transport.
conclusion: Tuning Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy can be used to control skyrmion motion, offering a potential mechanism for skyrmion-based devices.

title: Environment-dependent Tight-binding Models From ab Initio Pseudoatomic Orbital Hamiltonians
authors: M. Buongiorno Nardelli
abstract:
Author(s): M. Buongiorno Nardelli

Ab initio pseudoatomic orbital (PAO) Hamiltonians express the electronic structure of a solid in a compact, localized basis that spans the same Hilbert space as a conventional Slater-Koster tight-binding model, thereby providing an exact ab initio representation without any loss of accuracy. Buildin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045125] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to construct environment-dependent tight-binding models from ab initio pseudoatomic orbital Hamiltonians for electronic structure calculations.
motivation: To bridge the gap between first-principles accuracy and the computational efficiency of tight-binding models for large-scale simulations.
method: The authors derive a mapping from ab initio PAO Hamiltonians to a Slater-Koster tight-binding form, incorporating environment dependence through a self-consistent procedure.
result: The resulting tight-binding model reproduces the ab initio band structure and density of states with high accuracy for a range of materials.
conclusion: The approach provides an exact ab initio representation in a localized basis, enabling efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations for large systems.

title: Effect Of Modest Hydrostatic Pressure On Low-temperature Transport Behavior In ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Thin Films
authors: Deepak Kumar, Jared Z. Dans, Keenan E. Avers, Ryan Paxson, Ichiro Takeuchi, And Johnpierre Paglione

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055128] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of hydrostatic pressure on transport properties of La3Ni2O7 thin films, revealing a transition from Fermi liquid to non-Fermi liquid behavior.
motivation: To understand how strain and pressure can tune electronic states in bilayer nickelate thin films, potentially revealing exotic low-temperature phases.
method: Epitaxial thin films of La3Ni2O7 were grown under different substrate and oxygen conditions, then subjected to modest hydrostatic pressure while measuring transport properties.
result: Modest pressure drives a transition from Fermi liquid-like metallicity toward non-Fermi liquid response, indicating tunable transport behavior.
conclusion: Strain and pressure provide a pathway to control electronic states in bilayer nickelates, but the study is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Statistical Theory Of Electronic Degrees Of Freedom In Wave Packet Molecular Dynamics
authors: Daniel Plummer, Pontus Svensson, Wiktor Jasniak, Patrick Hollebon, Sam M. Vinko, And Gianluca Gregori
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Plummer, Pontus Svensson, Wiktor Jasniak, Patrick Hollebon, Sam M. Vinko, and Gianluca Gregori

We derive statistical distributions for the degrees of freedom in wave packet molecular dynamics models. Specifically, a theory is developed for the width distributions of Gaussian wave packets in both isotropic and anisotropic formulations. The resulting distribution functions show good agreement w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015219] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives statistical distributions for Gaussian wave packet widths in molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: To provide a theoretical foundation for the width parameters used in wave packet molecular dynamics models, which are important for simulating warm dense matter.
method: The authors develop a statistical theory for the width distributions of Gaussian wave packets in both isotropic and anisotropic formulations, likely using equilibrium statistical mechanics or maximum entropy principles.
result: The derived distribution functions show good agreement with numerical simulations, validating the theoretical approach.
conclusion: The work offers a predictive statistical description of electronic degrees of freedom in wave packet molecular dynamics, improving the modeling of warm dense matter.

title: Inferring Partial Crystalline Order In Liquids From Electrical Resistivity
authors: Nadine Wetta And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Nadine Wetta and Jean-Christophe Pain

This work investigates how locally persistent crystal-like ordering in liquids influences the Debye-Waller factor. We have developed a theoretical framework based on liquid-phonon theory which introduces a phonon relaxation time, expressed as the ratio of shear viscosity to infinite-frequency shear …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015220] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how persistent crystal-like ordering in liquids affects the Debye-Waller factor using liquid-phonon theory.
motivation: Understanding the influence of local crystalline order on liquid properties is important for condensed matter physics.
method: A theoretical framework based on liquid-phonon theory is developed, introducing a phonon relaxation time expressed as the ratio of shear viscosity to infinite-frequency shear modulus.
result: The framework shows how locally persistent ordering modifies the Debye-Waller factor.
conclusion: The work provides insights into partial crystalline order in liquids but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Role Of Stall Forces And Entropic Barriers In Geometry-dependent Polymer Translocation
authors: Reshmi Nayak, Damien Paul Foster, And Sanjay Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Reshmi Nayak, Damien Paul Foster, and Sanjay Kumar

We investigate the role of stall forces and entropic barriers in geometry-dependent polymer translocation through narrow pores. We consider two distinct geometrical constraints: forced translocation through a small pore in a flat membrane separating two semi-infinite three-dimensional spaces, and tr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015419] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polymer translocation through narrow pores under different geometrical constraints, focusing on stall forces and entropic barriers.
motivation: Understanding how geometry affects polymer translocation is important for biological and nanotechnological applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze forced translocation through a flat membrane pore and a conical pore.
result: They find that stall forces and entropic barriers play a key role in geometry-dependent translocation dynamics.
conclusion: The geometry of the pore significantly influences the translocation process, with implications for designing nanopore-based devices.

title: Variational Approach To Yukawa Fluids. I. Thermodynamics
authors: S. A. Khrapak And A. G. Khrapak
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Khrapak and A. G. Khrapak

The excess energy, entropy, and pressure of a strongly coupled Yukawa fluid are calculated from the variational approach using the fluid of hard spheres as a reference system. As in the case of the one-component plasma, the Percus-Yevick virial entropy is appropriate for such calculations and delive…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015216] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a variational hard-sphere reference system to compute thermodynamic properties of Yukawa fluids.
motivation: To provide an accurate and simple method for calculating excess energy, entropy, and pressure of strongly coupled Yukawa fluids.
method: A variational approach with a hard-sphere reference fluid and the Percus-Yevick virial entropy approximation.
result: The method yields accurate thermodynamic quantities for Yukawa fluids across a range of coupling parameters.
conclusion: The variational hard-sphere approach is effective for modeling Yukawa fluid thermodynamics.

title: Dynamics-induced Activity Patterns Of Active-inactive Clusters In Complex Networks
authors: Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

Synchrony patterns describe network states in which nodes of a coupled dynamical system are grouped into clusters based on synchronization between nodes. Beyond simple synchrony, synchronized clusters may also exhibit active or inactive states, and the collection of all such clusters constitutes an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014219] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies synchrony patterns and active-inactive cluster dynamics in complex networks, focusing on network science and nonlinear dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how synchronized clusters in coupled dynamical systems can exhibit active or inactive states is important for network dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model of coupled oscillators on complex networks, identifying conditions for active-inactive cluster patterns.
result: They find that network topology and coupling strength determine the emergence and stability of such activity patterns.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of synchrony in complex networks but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of step correlations.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into first-passage phenomena in superdiffusive processes, but it is not relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, and Ralf Metzler

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: To understand anomalous diffusion in complex media, particularly when transport is biased due to asymmetric distributions.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement and other transport characteristics using CTRW theory with coupled asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions.
result: They find that asymmetry in waiting-time and jump-length distributions leads to a rich variety of anomalous diffusion regimes, including subdiffusion, superdiffusion, and ballistic motion.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous systems.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in a thermosensitive neuronal network under electric fields, focusing on chimera states and traveling waves.
motivation: Understanding how electric fields affect neuronal network dynamics is important for neuromodulation and brain function.
method: Numerical simulations of a FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal network with hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields in a ring topology.
result: The network exhibits a range of collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera/multichimera states.
conclusion: Electric fields can induce complex spatiotemporal patterns in thermosensitive neuronal networks, with potential implications for neural information processing.

title: Realizable Entropic Lattice Boltzmann Method For high-Péclet Scalar Transport
authors: Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, And Xu Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, and Xu Chu

We present a realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method (RELBM) for scalar transport at high Péclet (Pe) number. The method combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with a nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a strictly conservative population-space realizability limiter activ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013301] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method for high-Péclet scalar transport, focusing on computational fluid dynamics.
motivation: To improve numerical stability and accuracy of lattice Boltzmann simulations for scalar transport at high Péclet numbers.
method: Combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a conservative realizability limiter.
result: The method achieves stable and accurate simulations for high-Péclet scalar transport.
conclusion: The proposed RELBM is effective for high-Péclet scalar transport problems in computational fluid dynamics.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices to quantify similarity between Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity of stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research.
method: The authors define a distance metric based on the spectral properties of stochastic matrices and compare it to existing measures.
result: The proposed distance function is shown to be a valid metric and outperforms alternatives in capturing structural differences between Markov chains.
conclusion: The distance function provides a useful tool for comparing stochastic processes, with potential applications in various fields.

title: Enhanced Multiphoton Ionization Driven By Quantum Light
authors: V. P. Kosheleva, S. Panahiyan, A. Rubio, And F. Schlawin
abstract:
Author(s): V. P. Kosheleva, S. Panahiyan, A. Rubio, and F. Schlawin

We present a first-principles [MATH]-matrix framework for multiphoton ionization driven by arbitrary quantum states of light, retaining the full spatial structure of the light fields. Within this framework, we show that the utilization of momentum-entangled photon pairs emitted by ultrathin nonlinear c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033106] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a first-principles S-matrix framework for multiphoton ionization driven by quantum light, showing that momentum-entangled photon pairs can enhance ionization yields.
motivation: To understand how quantum properties of light, such as entanglement, affect strong-field ionization processes beyond classical light descriptions.
method: The authors construct an S-matrix framework that incorporates the full spatial structure of arbitrary quantum states of light, and apply it to compute ionization rates for momentum-entangled photon pairs from ultrathin nonlinear crystals.
result: They find that momentum-entangled photon pairs can significantly enhance multiphoton ionization yields compared to classical or uncorrelated quantum light.
conclusion: Quantum light, particularly entangled photon pairs, offers a new control knob for strong-field ionization, with potential applications in quantum-enhanced spectroscopy and imaging.

title: Pulsed Optical Injection Steering In Multistable Semiconductor Laser Arrays Under Correlated Noise
authors: Max M. Chumley And Herbert G. Winful
abstract:
Author(s): Max M. Chumley and Herbert G. Winful

We demonstrate robust programmable state preparation in small Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) arrays with optical feedback using transient optical injection in the form of Gaussian pulses. In Lang-Kobayashi-type models of delay-coupled two- and three-laser arrays, multistability gives…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033112] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies programmable state preparation in VCSEL arrays using pulsed optical injection under correlated noise.
motivation: To achieve robust control of multistable laser arrays for applications in optical computing and communication.
method: Uses Lang-Kobayashi-type models with delay-coupled lasers and applies Gaussian optical injection pulses to steer between stable states.
result: Demonstrates that pulsed injection can reliably switch between states even in the presence of correlated noise.
conclusion: Pulsed optical injection is an effective method for state preparation in small VCSEL arrays, with potential for larger arrays.

title: Enhancing Optically Induced Intersite Spin Transfer In Antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic Ultrathin Films
authors: Ming-Shian Tsai, Li-Han Chang, Chun-Chia Tseng, Kunchala Ramesh Babu, Guang-Yu Guo, Bo-Yao Wang, And Ming-Chang Chen

Antiferromagnetic (AFM) films play a crucial role in advanced spintronic devices by regulating adjacent ferromagnetic (FM) layers via interfacial exchange coupling. However, the impact of antiferromagnets on magnetic dynamics of FM films under ultrashort laser pulses remains largely unknown. Using u…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033114] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optically induced spin transfer in antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic ultrathin films, focusing on spintronic device applications.
motivation: Understanding the impact of antiferromagnets on magnetic dynamics of ferromagnetic films under ultrashort laser pulses is crucial for advanced spintronic devices.
method: The authors use ultrafast optical techniques to investigate and enhance intersite spin transfer in antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic bilayer films.
result: They demonstrate enhanced optically induced spin transfer, revealing the role of antiferromagnetic layers in modulating magnetic dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing faster and more efficient spintronic devices using antiferromagnetic materials.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour
abstract:
Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce an exactly solvable population model in which cells grow exponentially with fluctuations that scale with the square …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exactly solvable stochastic population model with square-root growth noise and cell-size regulation, focusing on population dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems, which is a biological question.
method: The authors introduce a stochastic model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size, and solve it exactly.
result: The model yields exact analytical expressions for population growth statistics, revealing how noise and regulation interact.
conclusion: The work provides insights into stochastic population dynamics but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for applications in micro- and nano-electromechanical systems.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and classical molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer binding and sliding friction in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) contacts.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding energies and friction forces, enabling potential control of sliding resistance.
conclusion: External electric fields provide a viable route to control friction in layered materials like h-BN, which may have implications for nanoscale devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision-resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian
