method: Local protonic gating is applied to gate-defined homojunctions to induce a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect.
result: The method enables polarity-tunable, magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diode effects without magnetic fields, potentially useful for superconducting electronics.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques and optical antennas.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a metallic tip that acts as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field at the tip apex.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling fluorescence imaging of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical characterization of molecules and surfaces.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities induce forces and torques on particles, with applications in trapping and sorting.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including energy, momentum, and spin density analysis.
result: Unified description of forces and torques in both optics and acoustics, with applications in particle trapping, manipulation, and sorting.
conclusion: The review consolidates knowledge on radiation forces and torques, highlighting their importance in particle manipulation across optics and acoustics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open problems in modeling internal conversion.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods for internal conversion are needed to advance applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Valley-Engineered Landau Polaritons In A Van Der Waals Semiconductor Microcavity
authors: Xinyue Zhang, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Song Luo, Long Xu, Xin Li, Yuquan Zhou, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Zhao Xu, Haodong Cheng, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen
abstract:

title: Breaking The Speed Limit Of Chemical-Structure Imaging With Enhanced Force Sensitivity
authors: Yuuki Yasui And Yoshiaki Sugimoto

A new atomic force microscope captures the structures of individual molecules and their chemical bonds at record speeds.

motivation: To overcome the speed limitations of current chemical-structure imaging methods, enabling faster capture of molecular structures.
method: The authors developed an atomic force microscope with enhanced force sensitivity, allowing rapid scanning while maintaining high resolution.
result: The new microscope captures molecular structures and chemical bonds at record speeds, significantly faster than previous techniques.
conclusion: The enhanced force sensitivity enables a breakthrough in imaging speed, which could benefit studies of dynamic chemical processes.

title: Hyperfine-structure Constants Of The $^{45}\mathrm{Sc}$ Ii Ion And The Nuclear Quadrupole Moment
authors: Yong-Bo Tang, Yu-Shan Zhang, And Kai Wang

In this work, we calculate the hyperfine-structure constants of the [MATH] ion using a relativistic hybrid approach that combines configuration-interaction and coupled-cluster singles and doubles methods. Magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine-structure constants are deter…

motivation: Accurate hyperfine constants are needed for atomic spectroscopy and nuclear structure studies.

conclusion: The calculated values provide improved atomic data for Sc II.

title: Isotope Shifts In Heliumlike Carbon: Probes Of Nuclear Structure And New Bosons
authors: Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, and Ting-Yun Shi

We present high-precision calculations of isotope shifts for the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions in heliumlike [MATH], with mass-shift u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012817] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: High-precision calculations of isotope shifts in heliumlike carbon to probe nuclear structure and search for new bosons.
motivation: Isotope shifts provide a sensitive probe of nuclear properties and can constrain new physics beyond the Standard Model.

result: Accurate isotope shift parameters are obtained for the 1s2p 1P1 and 1s2s 3S1 transitions in C4+.
conclusion: The results enable improved nuclear charge radius determinations and set bounds on hypothetical bosonic particles.

title: Local Atomic Motifs In Halide Perovskite Alloys Reflect The Landscape Of Enthalpies And Band Gaps
authors: Fernando P. Sabino, Jia-Xin Xiong, Xiuwen Zhang, Gustavo M. Dalpian, And Alex Zunger
abstract:

Predicting the thermodynamic and electronic properties of halide perovskite (HP) alloys remains challenging due to their polymorphous character and the complex landscape of density-functional theory (DFT) calculated properties arising from local structural and chemical variations. Establishing clear…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024108] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies local atomic motifs in halide perovskite alloys and their correlation with enthalpies and band gaps using DFT calculations.
motivation: Predicting thermodynamic and electronic properties of halide perovskite alloys is challenging due to their polymorphous nature and complex DFT landscape.
method: The authors analyze local atomic motifs in halide perovskite alloys and correlate them with calculated enthalpies and band gaps using density-functional theory.
result: They find that local atomic motifs reflect the landscape of enthalpies and band gaps, providing insights into the structure-property relationships.
conclusion: Understanding local atomic motifs can help predict properties of halide perovskite alloys, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Computer Simulations Of The Stark Effect In The Helium-$β$ Complex Of Krypton In Inertial Confinement Fusion Conditions
authors: G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, And M. A. Gigosos

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.

title: Generating Consensus And Dissent On Massive Discussion Platforms With A Semantic-vector Model

Reaching consensus on massive discussion networks is critical for reducing noise and achieving optimal collective outcomes. However, the natural tendency of humans to preserve their initial ideas constrains the emergence of global solutions. To address this, collective intelligence (CI) platforms fa…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014311] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a semantic-vector model for generating consensus and dissent on massive discussion platforms, applied to collective intelligence.
motivation: To address the challenge of reaching consensus in large-scale online discussions where participants tend to preserve initial ideas, hindering global solutions.
method: The authors propose a semantic-vector model that represents opinions as vectors and simulates opinion dynamics to facilitate consensus or dissent.
result: The model demonstrates effectiveness in generating consensus or dissent on massive discussion platforms, as validated through simulations.
conclusion: The semantic-vector model offers a promising approach for managing collective decision-making in large online communities.

title: Theory Of Cell Body Lensing And Phototaxis Sign Reversal In “eyeless” Mutants Of Chlamydomonas
authors: Sumit Kumar Birwa, Ming Yang, Adriana I. Pesci, And Raymond E. Goldstein
abstract:

Phototaxis of many species of green algae relies upon directional sensitivity of their membrane-bound photoreceptors, which arises from the presence of a pigmented “eyespot” behind them that blocks light passing through the cell body from reaching the photoreceptor. A decade ago it was discovered th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014408] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phototaxis sign reversal in Chlamydomonas mutants lacking an eyespot, using a theoretical model of cell body lensing.
motivation: Understanding how eyeless mutants of Chlamydomonas can still exhibit phototaxis and sign reversal, challenging the conventional role of the eyespot.
method: The authors develop a ray-optics model of the cell body acting as a lens, combined with photoreceptor sensitivity, to predict phototactic behavior.
result: The model explains observed phototaxis sign reversal in eyeless mutants by accounting for cell body shape and refractive index.
conclusion: Cell body lensing is sufficient to explain phototaxis in eyeless mutants, providing insight into the minimal requirements for directional light sensing.

authors: Morteza Dejam And Hassan Hassanzadeh

The solute transport due to mixed electro-osmotic and pressure-driven flows of viscoelastic fluids in microchannels is studied here. The Reynolds decomposition technique, in combination with the assumptions underlying the Taylor-Aris theory, is used to derive a reduced-order model that yields the di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015105] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies solute transport in mixed electro-osmotic and pressure-driven flows of viscoelastic fluids in microchannels using a reduced-order model.
motivation: Understanding solute transport in microfluidic devices is important for applications like lab-on-a-chip, but viscoelastic fluids add complexity.

result: The model yields the dispersion coefficient as a function of fluid rheology and flow parameters.
conclusion: The reduced-order model accurately predicts solute transport in viscoelastic flows, aiding microfluidic design.

motivation: To understand how flexible fibers influence the free-surface flow of granular materials, which is unexplored.
method: Experimental investigation of dry granular flows with added flexible fibers, measuring avalanche dynamics.
result: Flexible fibers alter the bulk mechanical strength and flow behavior of granular media.
conclusion: The addition of fibers significantly affects granular avalanches, with implications for material reinforcement.

title: Wettability-mediated Transition From Circular To Radial Cracks In Dried Deposit Of Colloidal Ellipsoids
authors: Sanket Kumar, Madivala G. Basavaraj, And Dillip K. Satapathy

We report a transition in the orientation of primary cracks in colloidal ellipsoid deposits driven exclusively by variations in substrate wettability. motivation: Understanding crack formation in colloidal deposits is important for applications like coatings and inkjet printing, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: On wettable substrates cracks are circular; on less wettable substrates they become radial.
conclusion: Substrate wettability can control crack orientation in colloidal ellipsoid deposits.

Constant-intensity (CI) waves are plane-wave-like solutions that are known to propagate in non-Hermitian inhomogeneous media with complex external potential (with the real part corresponding to the refractive index and the imaginary part representing a distribution of gain and loss) while keeping th…

tldr: This paper studies constant-intensity waves and modulational instability in a higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a real potential, which is a topic in nonlinear optics and wave propagation.

conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of electronic structure in these materials but do not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

We introduce a minimal multiscale framework that links within-host virus dynamics to population-level susceptible-infectious-recovered-susceptible (SIRS) epidemiology through explicit, bidirectional coupling. At the microscopic layer, a two-variant quasispecies (master and mutant genomes with packag…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033097] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper models viral evolution and epidemic dynamics using a multiscale framework coupling within-host quasispecies dynamics with population-level SIRS epidemiology.
motivation: To understand how within-host viral evolution and population-level epidemic dynamics mutually influence each other, which is important for predicting viral emergence and spread.
method: The authors develop a minimal multiscale model that couples a two-variant quasispecies model (master and mutant) at the within-host level with a SIRS model at the population level, incorporating bidirectional feedback.
result: The model shows that multiscale feedback can lead to complex dynamics such as oscillatory behavior and affect the emergence and persistence of viral variants.
conclusion: Multiscale coupling is crucial for accurately modeling viral evolution and epidemic dynamics, and the framework can be extended to study other pathogens.

Heterogeneous nucleation at surface edges is pervasive across nature and industry, yet the role of line pinning effect, arising from asymmetric capillary interactions at geometric singularities, remains poorly understood. Herein, we develop a generalized nucleation theory that explicitly incorporate…

title: Programming Stability And Stiffness In Two-dimensional Multistable Structures

result: They demonstrate programmable control over stability and stiffness in the fabricated structures.
conclusion: The framework enables design of adaptive materials with tailored mechanical properties.

title: Rheology Of Dense Vibrated Granular Flows: Nonmonotonic Response Controlled By Granular Temperature
authors: A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, And E. Lippiello
abstract:
Author(s): A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, and E. Lippiello

When subjected to vibrations, the effective viscosity of a granular medium depends heavily on both confining pressure and vibration parameters. In this work, experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer are used to provide a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations. The results show that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by the granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032010] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheology of dense vibrated granular flows, focusing on the nonmonotonic response controlled by granular temperature.
motivation: Understanding the effective viscosity of granular media under vibrations is important for industrial processes and geophysics, but a unified framework reconciling experimental observations is lacking.
method: The authors use experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer to model dense vibrated granular flows.
result: They find that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.
conclusion: The study provides a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations of granular rheology under vibrations.

title: Constraints On The Thomson Optical Depth To The Cosmic Microwave Background From The Lyman-$α$ Forest
authors: Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, And James S. Bolton

motivation: To test large values of the optical depth suggested by recent data.
method: Analysis of high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest spectra from distant QSOs.
result: Mild tension with large optical depth values, consistent with Planck satellite measurements.
conclusion: The Lyman-alpha forest provides a useful independent constraint on the Thomson optical depth.

title: Intermittency-driven Subcritical Fiber Breakage In Turbulence

result: Intermittency significantly reduces the critical length compared to mean-field predictions, making fibers more prone to breakage.
conclusion: Turbulent intermittency must be accounted for to accurately predict fiber fragmentation in realistic flows.

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi

Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, revealing hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and reducing this noise requires detailed knowledge of coating material properties.
method: The authors used experimental techniques such as Brillouin light scattering and spectroscopic ellipsometry to characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films.
result: They discovered that the films exhibit hidden anisotropy that is not eliminated by standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating design and postprocessing.
conclusion: The findings inform strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects and electrical stress.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments, highlighting recent advances from BESIII.
result: BESIII has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems with high-precision data.
conclusion: The study of open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders continues to be a primary source of experimental information for hadron spectroscopy and strong interaction physics.

abstract:

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo radar significantly advanced characterization of near-Earth asteroids and provided unique insights into planetary surfaces and subsurfaces.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary science, and its loss leaves a gap in observational capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on various fields of astronomy.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific achievements from the telescope's operation.
result: Highlights major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave background detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades enabled sustained scientific breakthroughs over five decades until its collapse.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews geospace science advances using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere and ionosphere have enabled significant advances in geospace science, which this Colloquium aims to summarize.
method: The paper reviews key results obtained with Arecibo's incoherent scatter radar, lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, covering plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The review highlights advances in understanding ionospheric plasma processes, atomic metal layers, and coupling between the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace research, and its legacy continues to inform current and future studies of the upper atmosphere.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies using convection-cloud chambers that reproduce turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation.
result: Convection-cloud chambers provide controlled conditions to study key processes bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but the paper does not involve quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on modeling and detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and gravitational waves provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents the latest modeling results and signal predictions, highlighting the potential for multimessenger observations.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from core collapse supernovae, combined with photons and neutrinos, will significantly advance our understanding of supernova physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is important for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave events (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to theoretical nuclear equation of state models.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are presented, showing consistency with some nuclear models but leaving uncertainties at high densities.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, testing the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale distribution of matter with the CMB dipole.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by examining a significant inconsistency between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole anisotropy and compare it with the CMB dipole, including assessment of biases and systematic issues.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observational signatures.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test beyond-standard-model physics through astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical models of self-interacting dark matter and comparison with observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent experimental results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search strategies, and project sensitivities for the High-Luminosity LHC across multiple channels.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and estimates of discovery reach for the HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain regions, and the HL-LHC will significantly extend the search sensitivity.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental work from the last decade on nuclear reactions, plasma physics, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: It provides an updated understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning and its diagnostic probes.
conclusion: The paper advances the model of the solar interior but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, focusing on fluid mechanics.
result: Key insights include the effects of added mass, deformable surfaces, turbulence, and surfactants on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive overview to guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, bridging the gap between optical and ultrasound imaging.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches enhancing its capabilities.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding morphological instabilities in soft materials is important for materials science and biology, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and nonlinear elasticity to analyze the Biot instability.
result: It provides a modern treatment of buckling phenomena in soft matter, including creases and cusps.
conclusion: The paper is a valuable resource for soft matter physics but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
